b1-p002.t: Lost... I've been driving too long.
"It watched the twin beams twist and turn up the dangerously circuitous route..."

b1-p003.t: At the point when the driver was most assured, he had lost complete control.
Nothing stirred for a long time. Then someone descended from the tree.

b1-p004.t: He had been staring at the ceiling for a long time before he realized he was awake.
His weakened arm found the glass too heavy and spilled most of the water...
He sat up. The plaster on his right arm. His legs intact. The room was \not clinical...
The brilliance of sunlight blinded him momentarily...
The room opened into a large wonderfully sunlit courtyard.
A study! There were books everywhere. As if antiquity was preserved there, albeit a bit haphazardly.
Window panes revealed the reflection of a bearded face with a heavily bandaged head
The reflection of a stranger. He collapsed with a swoon, knocking artefacts over as he hit the hard floor.

b1-p005.t: Summer was at its peak. The professor had been planting trees, despite the drought. 'They are always around when you want to talk to someone,' he would say.
Now, now professor! Must you really plant trees when people are dying of thirst?
A man stood under the kadamba tree, raving that the Gods are angry.
The villagers pelted him with stones until he died. Fear descended... because they knew hatred was amongst them.

b1-p006.t: How does the wounded one do?
Of course he sleeps. I have seen everything. I predicted the exact date of his arrival.
Oh, him? He's fine. I can't be sure. He's not woken up, really."
A temple is to be constructed. The foundation ceremony is exactly two weeks from now. The Wounded One MUST attend.
The Wounded One with No Past will become our saviour!
Read it, professor, and burn the date in this muddled head of yours!
I am forced to return indoors, as the sun is overhead and my hat is missing.

b1-p007.t: She is Varahi, one of the saptamatrikas. Her fourth arm would have formed the abhay-mudra but that is missing. It was found damaged when Kurup found it in the ancient temples.
You were in a coma. It's impossible to find anything intact, really, including our history.
Because of the accident, I should think. Must you fret about those things when we are in the midst of such secret knowledge?
Read these books, my young friend, for they will help you put together your past.
Why? Why was I in a coma??
I am Doctor Vidyasagar Parthasarathi, owner of this room and the rest of the lodge.What's your name? Come on, out with it.
And he collapsed for the second time in the same day.

b1-p008.t: The decaying magnificence of the building - a relic of the raj, a symmetrical square squatting in the middle of sprawling environs.
He could see someone up ahead. Sun made the figure a dark silhouette surrounded by brilliance.
That is a well! A very deep well!
Are you? You already died once.
You mean my accident? So you know about me?

b1-p009.t: Everyone around here knows about you. You're The Wounded One with No Past, right?
I can't remember. The knock on the head must have done it. That’s what the doctor said.
Doctor Parthasarathi. The old man who lives here. Likable, but loony. Do you know him?
Do I know a loony old Dr. Parthasarathi? Can't be sure about that.
Why have you come to this valley? Nobody ever comes here anymore. Why did you?

b1-p010.t: Are you really an incarnation, sahib?
Back inside, sounds could be heard coming from the kitchen.
Mahantji is very learned, sahib. If he has said you are an incarnation, then you must be.
People are scared of Mahantji. But I do not fear anyone above God. Mahantji is an evil man. He has many vices.
Tell me about this valley. What is this place? Where are we?
All I know is that we are in a valley surrounded by mountains.
We went by train, then bus, then car up and down the hills. I was so sick I threw up and slept. I don't know how we got here. But once I did, I have never gone out.
How does one go out from this valley?

b1-p011.t: You will not leave us, sahib?
There are wild animals! Nagas in the forests, and Yakshas hide in the trees. Nobody dares, sahib
He could not respond. Somewhere beyond the mountains that surrounded the valley hid his past, his identity.
That's a good piece of land you've chosen there, Mahant.
All governed by divya vaastu. The Lord dictates what he wants.
Mahant surveyed the temple site from the shade. Outside, sweltering in the midday sun, volunteers cleansed the land in the ritual Shalyodhara.
Faith needs miracles. He is my miracle. A fool who dropped into my lap like a blessing.
Why do we need this wounded guy? Who is he anyway?
The Wounded One will have to forget everything else and don a new avatar.
Le’ts raise a toast to that!
The common man knows the truth but is powerless. His silent disapproval speaks volumes.

b1-p012.t: Dr. Parthasarathi, have you seen a loony old man around here?
I can't say that I have. Why do you ask?
Thank you doctor for treating me.
I am a mere professor. Bhavi is the doctor. She fixed you up, my boy.
Here, have this panchamrita. It will invigorate your very soul.
You are an anomaly, young man. I do not accept prophecies, but you are a singularity forcing me to question my utmost beliefs.
Name? You do need a name! I have it. We will call you Dvij, young man, for you are twice- born!
I think you are pretending. This is all planned by that evil Mahant. He bought you with money. This is an evil scheme, uncle. We have to stop it!
She fears for my safety, and rightly so. Sometimes what you do can become your undoing. At other times, it's simply because of what you know.

b1-p013.t: Does it hurt? Good. It might force you to remember things.
The scar will remain. It will go well with that wounded image you are supposed to carry.
Will you stop bickering with your only patient and answer the door?
She's a firebrand, my niece. The wild berries have poisoned her tongue.
it's the Mahant's henchman. He wants the Wounded One to attend some ceremony at the main temple. Today! Guess word must have traveled that the Wounded One is Wounded No More.
It's the cowherd who gets the milk. He spreads the word around.
Am I not supposed to know everything? I am the Wounded One after all.

b1-p014.t: No doubt you know by now that I predicted your arrival in this valley, and that you would arrive wounded.
Yes, of course I know. It is as per His divine plan. You will fulfill your duties. Now I shall give you my blessings.
Yes, O wise one. Just like you predicted, I have lost my memory. Without my memory I have no past.
You shall have a new name. And that shall be...
Dvij, name me Dvij, O holy one.

b1-p015.t: Come, sit by my side. Let the people see you sitting with me.
He faithfully followed all orders. By the end, Mahant was immensely pleased with how Dvij had conducted himself.
Now go and wait till I give the word to come back, on the night when the new moon will dawn.
Dvij walked across the barren land, satisfied with his performance. Soon his thoughts turned to his missing past, which hid somewhere beyond the tall mountains that encircled this unknown valley.

b1-p016.t: An army of mules crossed the bridge, carrying heavy loads of brick and pebbles for the planned temple construction.
A few days later, Dvij went in search of Viraat, the delivery man who brought supplies from over the mountains.
A tavern stood at the crossroads of two dusty paths. A tumbledown shack, half brick, half bamboo and thatch.
Inside it, Dvij found the milkman chatting with his friends.
I know you talk to Maharaj. Speak up.
This skeleton of a man is Viraat?
What do you want? I can get it only next Wednesday!

b1-p017.t: I don’t want anything. Rather, I want to give you gifts. Take anything from my car.
You want me to have your things because I brought you down?
That, and to take me back up there.
You don't want me to go to the mukhiya and tell him what inflated rates you charge? You are misusing your monopoly.
What? Impossible! I can't do that!
The slope is much steeper going out. My van will never bear both our weights.
I still can't believe you use this to carry loads over the mountains!
I’m worried about the fading sunlight. It’ll be night soon.

b1-p018.t: What are you so worried about?
Banmanus! And pichhal peris, pishachas, kimpurushas, kinnars
Age-old legends, fabricated to scare children from straying into forests. Now used by Mahant to scare peasants from escaping.
Night falls quickly in the mountains. The shadows of trees on one side reached midway up the trunks on the other side.
There! That's where I found you. But we can't stop now.
Dvij kept looking at the scene of crash till it was out of his sight.

b1-p019.t: Suddenly the engine seized up, spluttered wildly and came to a standstill.
Grab a bigger rock to make it stop!
They jammed a large boulder behind the wheel, moments before the van was about to roll off a cliff.
Dvij found himself a milestone to sit on. Closest place was 129 km. Nothing close enough to traverse on foot.
The accident spot was a site of carnage. The car's front was bashed in, headlights gone and front tires busted.
The seatbelt is intact. I must not have been wearing it. The key's still in the ignition.

b1-p020.t: I am scared. Can I come in with you?
What I found surprising was that you were undressed. Your clothes were lying by your side with blood on them.
I was WHAT?! You mean I was naked... like completely?
How did you manage to take them off? And why?
Strange memories flashed in his mind.
The brakes are gone, and so is the gearbox. Steering wheel is jammed. Keep your arms and legs in. We are going to make it to the bottom.
They wrenched off the broken bumper. Dvij gave one to Viraat, keeping the other as he climbed into the moving car.
I will never, ever, do that again.

b1-p021.t: Now Mahant will know and you will be in trouble.
Oh uncle! It was all a dumb act. It was meant to fail from the beginning!
I’d love to stay in the valley - if only you stop making these allegations.
Now Viraat is stuck, all because of you. Who will bring supplies?
Viraat will be fine. I told him to take the engine belt from my car to replace his broken one.
Mahant has expectations from you, my boy.
I know. He said that himself before yesterday's ceremony.
I met Mahant in a tent at the temple site. There were a couple of other guys.
Baldev and Vaid! These 3 are always cooking some evil plan!
They had some sort of a diagram for the temple.
Was the diagram anything like this?

b1-p022.t: A giant man, the Vaastu Purusha, once roamed the void and confronted the Gods. Threatened, they attacked together and pinned it down. Facing down, the Vaastu Purusha supports the entire universe!
It became the sacred blueprint for temple architecture, for towns, for homes. Each level a miniature version of the level above... like fractals... cosmos within a cosmos.
But I am surprised. Mahant allowed you to return. Why?
He asked me to wait till he sends word for the big ceremony. The thing is... I don't intend to.
How do you plan to get out?
By studying that map. There must be a way out of here.
Yes! Study the map. I need fresh legs to fetch artifacts for my research.

b1-p023.t: Several days later, when the wounds had healed...
They walked aimlessly through the Jambuvan forest, outskirts lined with tall trees and sparse undergrowth, intermittent clearings densely populated with tall grass.
These are offerings made by the tribes. They think these signposts are signs with mystical meanings, left over from the ages of Gods.
Come along, or I will leave you to find your own way out of here!
Because you love your uncle too much. You will not let me out of your sight.
I came here many years ago when this place was opened to tourists. My father worked for the national park. The first few years were amazing...
Then that day happened. Uncle picked me up early and bolted us us in. I kept asking for my mom and dad. They never came back.
They went missing that day. Much later uncle told me they had been killed.

b1-p024.t: I don’t know. But he certainly wishes evil. I will not let anything happen to my Uncle..
You think Mahant was behind it?
I understand why you hate me. You think I'm here to hurt your uncle. I shudder to think my memory might return and prove I really came to hurt him.
This valley of yours...its unreal...forgotten by the world, with no connectivity, no means to escape...
full of strange people with stranger stories.
Nothing as strange as you arriving on the exact date Mahant predicted, yet claiming to have no idea why.
You must think I'm a total dumb to believe that.
I had an almost fatal accident. You said so yourself. It's perfectly possible to lose memory after an accident like that.
What about my problems? I have no idea who I am, stuck in a strange place with strange people who all want something from me.
It's also perfectly possible to make up a story. I don't care either which way the truth lies.
YOUR problems? You're a crook placed by Mahant to spy on my uncle's research!
Me a SPY? Spying on what? Prof's BOOK COLLECTION?
Now look what you have done. You've made me lose my way

b1-p025.t: Run, Bhavi... run for your life.
You are scared of HIM? Why, he's a Soma. The friendliest flock of people in the valley.
They are intrepid honey collectors through the ages. They learned dhokra casting when the park did well. Their images were in great demand.
Soma tribe lived deep into the forest heart, where low-lying kuchcha huts lined a clearing in a circle of tall trees.
That's their leader? Maybe time to elect someone new.
No silly. He's a shaman. Soma God descends onto him in trance. Watch what he'll do.
A man ran out gesticulating wildly, then stood firm making wild contortions of his upper body parts, like a man possessed.

The shaman kept wild movements to increasing tempo, in a trance of ecstatic oblivion. Without lifting his feet, he gradually inched toward the large casket and started drinking a liquid with distinctive color.

b1-p026.t: Shh! Quiet! It's sacrilege to disturb the shaman in trance. That's Soma. The drink of the Gods.
The shaman unnaturally kept pace. His head swung as if unhinged. Everyone stood mesmerized - witnessing cosmic creation dance...
Is he doing what I'm thinking he's doing?
So that wild dance was about answering the call of nature?
Stop the wisecracks! He's a human filter. His body absorbs the potent poisons, making the drink safe for others.
A sober man drank the filtered liquid ceremonially. The effect was instantaneous - he swayed, transforming.
Chaos erupts as masses pour in.
Why imagine when one can experience.

b1-p027.t: That's funny... I don't recall seeing the sun rise this side before.
That's because it's sunset! You slept through the day!
You won't believe the kick that stuff gives. And no hangover. No wonder they call it the drink of the Gods!
Do you remember that you had to be carried back! You with your horrible breath. We tripped three times!
And do you recall... what you said to me?
I can't understand what made me say that. It must have been the drink. I'm really sorry!
Did I say anything? Did I? Did I ask you if you...
That dark, beautiful face in his dreams. Was it her? A faint smile stretched across his lips as he headed to the Professor's study.
Professor sat deep in thought, manuscripts spread across his desk. He started upon seeing Dvij.

b1-p028.t: I've been informed you experienced Soma's effects. How was it?
Uncle! You're justifying what he did?!
Yes! Soma... somatic... psychosomatic! Consider yourself blessed!
Of course! Soma is one of the many great discoveries of our forefathers.
But Soma is just one of them. Our great maharishis knew of many secrets. For example kust take...
But the drink is too potent for ordinary mortals. It takes a possessed shaman to filter out the toxic agents.
...the great Panini! He encapsulated entire grammar in so few rules! Even by a vast arrays of computers cannot do a better job! Just look at this example—
But I digress again. I have translated many works. I also happen to have brought into my possession knowledge of an ancient art that would be extremely valuable to whoever lays their hands on it.

But that knowledge must not fall into wrong hands. Therefore I have done it in the most ingenious manner. I have left clues, all over the place. Most ingenious clues they are. I challenge you...to find them.
Not in the house, my child. All over the valley.
You should know. You've been reading my little black book.

b1-p029.t: The path wound through the fortress in sharp bends - a ruse to mislead invading armies into apparent dead-ends.
They say some people were buried alive within these walls.
They started the search for clues with Daundagarh fort. A huge fortress wall loomed before them, ramparts of cut-stone speaking of medieval might and lost kingdoms.
No. Poor, innocent people. The spirits of the dead would keep the walls from giving away.
After crossing five massive gates, they reached an open plateau. A small temple stood among scattered ruins.
That's a group of shatavari plants. Very popular with local womenfolk.
Shatavari means 'one who has a hundred husbands.'

b1-p030.t: Soldiers were made to climb here laden with armaments. Some claim cavalry rode horses up. A test of skill and fitness.
How are you able to climb so quickly?
From the tower's edge, the entire valley spread below. Massive boulders scattered everywhere spoke of ancient mysteries.
I would have thought Mahant would hire a more robust guy.
Yesterday you didn't want me around. Today you have me roaming with you. Change of heart?
The myth says giants lived here. A legend tells of rakshasa Vraktaasura riding a mountain to fight Indra, who struck it down with his vajra. These boulders are the shattered remains.
Don't even think about it. I only want you away from my uncle.
How can we know if that is true?
Scientists deride ancient beliefs as myths...
Or it could be that an asteroid broke apart right above, scattering pieces across the hill.

b1-p031.t: ...but their explanations are equally madcap sometimes. Most often it's a toss-up what to believe.
I believe a drop of rain just pattered on my head.
First showers of the season! I hope they last. Quick, hit the covers!

They ran across the fort's ramparts like soldiers once did when the fort came under attack - this time fleeing not arrows, but rain. They scampered through the rain to an isolated temple, seeking shelter as the storm intensified.
Don't bother trying. No cellphone towers around. Did you check messages and pics?
I did. Messages, contacts, even pictures. But I don't recall any of the names or photos.
That's been the problem. The rains stop before they even start. Who’s this girl?

b1-p032.t: See this. Looks like etched by hand.
If I told you that, I'd hardly hold on to my claim of memory loss.
I think it's a pasha, a weapon of one of the Gods. I saw a drawing of it in Prof's black book.
Looking for ways to have another accident?
Hey, look at that tank ? Simply breathtaking.
It's a pushkarini - a sacred place for ceremonial bathing. There's a fun way down there. Follow me.
They bent low to crawl through an underpass across the channel that flowed into the tank.

b1-p033.t: Smooth rounded pebbles jostled in the clear water.

Bhavi rolled up her salvar and stepped into the cool stream, gesturing for Dvij to join her. They walked upstream, their feet rolling over rounded stones, conscious of the other's presence, afraid to join hands - long, precious moments suspended in time.

The next day they walked towards the village. The ten Mahavidhya temples stood closed during lunch hour, when through the priests the Gods took their food. Children stood beneath mango trees hoping the rain had dislodged fruit.
What is that old woman doing? Why is there nobody around to help her?
Leprosy. Nobody would dare go near that hut.
At the village outskirts lived the avarna - outcastes beyond even the varna system. The pratilomas, made of substance with misaligned grains.

b1-p034.t: You are a doctor. Can't you do anything?
I tried to set up shop. Initially some villagers came. But then Mahant and Vaid branded my practice as witchcraft.
The old womanlooked at him with reverence and suddenly clutched his wrist. A sense of having accomplished something good overpowered him as he patted her gnarled fingers.
Are you crazy? How could you let her touch you?
How could I forget. You are the Wounded One. The savior.
You said I have nothing to fear. I have died once already.
Villagers started following them at reverent distance. Ponga, the blabbering fool, broke from ranks to follow closely.
Now I'm beginning to get scared of the crowd.
Oh so the savior wants to be saved? Follow me.
Not of the forest. Of what resides in it.
Wild animals. Some tribes. But most of all fear itself, invented by those who do not want the villagers to step out of the village.
They snaked through narrow alleys, and suddenly entered dense vegetation. The pattering feet behind them stopped at the forest edge.

b1-p035.t: Mahant was rudely roused from his mid-afternoon sleep by the commotion in the streets. The idea of a large crowd gathering without him addressing them was reprehensible. He walked to the jharokha overlooking the main bazaar street.
That girl is a bad influence on Dvij. A few more days and we shall have the biggest ceremony that will make people forget everything else.
Normally he would address gatherings from this window. Today he just watched till Dvij and Bhavi disappeared.
I told you to go away!!
Another knock sounded - softer. The door creaked open.
I know where it is. I will have my hands on it any day now.
A mahari entered, taking lustful steps forward but stopped seeing Baldev. Mahant flicked his fingers and she disappeared as quickly as she'd appeared.
Ah Kurup! You come when I am in a good mood. Tell me, what news do you bring?
What you should worry about is when I will have my hands on it.
Three days, Kurup, three days. That is all you shall have. Now leave.
This time it was Kurup - his grotesque features contrasting with the splendor of a beautiful muthi he was carrying.

b1-p036.t: The Forest Officer's bungalow stood abandoned, overgrown, bathed in eerie sunset light - a bhoot bungalow with a sinister reputation.
Nobody in their senses goes in there.
Wouldn't that make it the perfect spot to hide a clue?
They climbed the wall, circled through overgrown shrubs, and entered through a broken window that opened with a reverberating rankle.
Doesn't that remind you of the cinema of the sixties?
Nothing reminds me of anything I remember.

b1-p037.t: Dvij's light fell upon a gun collection which he examined carefully, one weapon at a time.
You found files? That should be the park's records.
The visitor numbers only go up. The park couldn't have been closed for lack of money.
So that story was planted to hide something else. Some sinister business I'm sure.
Look at this statue. I press its arm and...bingo! It's not that paperweight.
That bookcase...it opened when I picked up this paperweight!
Moonlight! That's it. We will use the moonlight.
A mirror fixed to a dressing table positioned correctly directed the the silvery light moonlight into the darkness.
Why would there be a tunnel under the Forest Officer's bungalow?

b1-p038.t: Could that be one of your parents?
His skull is fractured, right through the calvaria. He was hit from above with something heavy. Then left here to be eaten by worms.
Whoever did this would have gone out the other end of the tunnel. Let us find where it leads.
The phone died. They groped through darkness until finding steps leading up to a chained opening with slivers of moonlight.
The morgue! That must be the Kaal Bhairava temple! The tantric! Could he?
Looks like we are near some temple.
That we'll know only when we talk to him. But that can only be after I've slept through yet another morning.
I still can't believe you thought that skeleton was one of my parents.

b1-p039.t: Why the boots, Bhavi? Are you going anywhere special? Could it be... the Kaal Bhairava temple?
Why, that is a good idea. You must show that magnificent architecture to Dvij!
Next day, the sky was overcast and gloomy, even as late as when Dvij finally woke up. Professor played a board game with himself.
They are devotees of Lord Shiva as Bhairava...the destroyer. They practice extreme ritual worship. Challenge not their beliefs.
Kaal Bhairava temple stood mystifying, appearing to float on Bhootnath taal with densely forested Naga hill behind. Vultures circled above the cremation ground.
Ferocious vyalas flanked the steps - composite creatures controlling cosmic energy. The soft stone from Naga hill bore delicate carvings of gods, beasts, and flowers.

b1-p040.t: Inside, pillars carved with water symbols rose toward heaven. Sadhus meditated before the swayamshiva lingam, kapalas beside them.
They waited in the adjunct room until Baba emerged from Samadhi.
You are The Wounded One with No Past. Your business is with the Mahant. Why do you seek my audience?
They bowed before Baba - vibhuti on his forehead, bhasma on his body, wisdom in his eyes. His voice was sonorous, his manner firm yet hearty.
You are a great Siddhi Nath, O revered Baba. Please do not humiliate us by asking the reason of our visit.
You have come to seek advice on something concerning others more than you.
Yes, that is true. I have come to you to understand your path to God.
Very well! But the path is only for true believers for it will ask you to challenge everything you believe today. Are you willing?
I understand that true knowledge hides in darkness. in deep, dark tunnels under the belly of earth. I desire to seek that knowledge.
Baba standing up and beginning to walk around Dvij and Bhavi in a circle - peripatetic teaching style.

b1-p041.t: I understand what you imply. The Kaula traditions. How poorly understood by miserable disbelievers.
What would be those secret rituals, O divine Nath?
You are not ready for that knowledge. Secret rituals are extremely potent, only after years of practicing asanas and samadhis. He shall demonstrate to silence your incredulity.
What he will demonstrate is the Khechari Mudra...a small ritual and yet extremely potent.

The sadhu opened wide and snaked his tongue back into his throat. It did not stop where a normal person's would. Their eyes widened as it kept going in, till the whole thing disappeared inside the cavernous mouth.
The tongue has been pulled up between the eyes...inside the amakala. This is to stop the nectar of immortality dripping away.
You seek knowledge of secret rituals. And yet, nothing is secret in my ashram.

b1-p042.t: You no longer hear me. But I am not offended. I see who has caught your attention. She has the enchantment of Tripura Sundari herself.
I have named her Kamakhya. She is a Naga tribal - fiercely proud, wary of strangers.
But this one has taken a liking to you.
Very well! If it has happened then so it must be. I have come to understand that you have mingled with her already...
...though you may not recall it. She desires to be yours and I have granted her the boon.
You do not have a choice. She has tasted your blood. You are already inside her.
I am honoured, O mystic. But I do not believe I can be a yogi till my task here is done. Only then shall I be able to take a yogini.

b2-p001.t: Hardly repulsive, don’t you think? Besides, she saved my life.
What, when she drank your blood? That’s not repulsive? Who does that?
Will that repulsive creature follow us wherever we go?
I doubt that. It's all part of your plan, isn't it? Say it!
Bhavi quickly closed the door behind her, then watched from the window.
Has that man gone mad, Bhavi? He makes less sense than I do.
Bhavi's shadow, Professor. It feels vulnerable here.
The only time he makes sense, uncle, is when he is lying.

b2-p002.t: Tell me, my boy, besides making incoherent remarks, what else did you gather from your visit to the marvelous temple?
Dvij gave a short account of their visit to the temple and interaction with the tantric baba, skipping only the part about the mysterious yogini.
You enquired the aghori about kaula traditions? You never ask someone their innermost secrets. You have to become them.
The Nagas. Where do they fit into this scheme of things?
The Nagas are ardent aghori followers. They have suffered much. The men butchered and women abused by centuries of civilized settlers. That tribe is like a wounded tiger eager to avenge.
The aghoris possess, in a sense, a fondness for objects otherwise considered repulsive.
Have you gone totally mad, young man?
Sorry professor! You were talking about aghoris’ fondness for repulsive creatures.
I've been jumpy off late. Even a knock on the door gives me jitters. Wait! That reminds me. There was a knock.

b2-p003.t: Hopefully after 10 am. Otherwise the audience will find their chief guest snoring.
Don't be silly. Brahmakaal always begins at 4 a.m.
A messenger from Mahant. He reminded The Wounded One with No Past to be present at the garbhadhana ceremony beginning this evening. Shubh muhurat for the garbhadhana is at Brahmakaal
I'll have to be up the whole night?
Professor explained the history of Shayani Ekadashi.
Do I really have to go?
Of course you do. Why, I insist. In fact, I will join you.
Nonsense! Mere difference of opinion. It's decided. I shall accompany you at Brahmakaal.
You, uncle? I thought you did not like Mahant.
My clues! You should have traversed the whole valley looking for clues. Have you not?
We did but could not find a thing, uncle! We need help!
This secret...its knowledge will bring dangers. I have felt them. I cannot let you be under any risk.
And yet she needs to know the secret or the knowledge will be lost.
Can you give at least one more clue?
Ok, here’s one. Look for directions...to indescribable wealth

b2-p004.t: What do you think...was the tantric babainvolved in the killing?
The warm glow from the burning diya enacted a dance of shadows on the walls. Bhavi had explained the dining hall was on a separate power phase that had stopped working long ago.
You’re right! Why would they leave it in the tunnel?
No. If the tunnel led to aghori;s ashraam, they would have buried the skeleton in the cremation ground.
"Now I understand why you shouted 'skeletons'! Did we make a mistake figuring direction from moonlight?
The mirror! The dressing table was turned halfway.
That's true. It was at about 45 degrees to the bookshelf.
Since the moon was on the west, the tunnel must have gone north-west. That means the temple we saw was the...
I'll be meeting him in a few hours. I'll try to confront him.
So it turns out to be Mahant after all.

b2-p005.t: I'll never believe you. You're a scheming fiend. Even your shadow shows it.
You will question the man who employed you? How gullible do you think I am?
I better get some sleep if I have to wake up at all
Professor had started seeing shadows lurking about the lodge. Hearing strange sounds.
I can't take the risk anymore. I have to act now.
He pulled shutters over windows, walked quickly to his desk, and began drawing cryptic images on parchment - meaningless to the wrong eyes, invaluable to the right ones.

When he was done, he folded the parchment neatly and dropped it in his overcoat pocket. Then wearing the same coat, he dropped himself across the sofa without closing the light. He lay awake, waiting.

b2-p006.t: The proposed temple ground was invisible under a sea of humanity. The entire village was there, mixing and mingling in excited chatter. Early evening sun bore down heavily, occasional dark clouds providing welcome respite.
Peasants flocked to the bazaar where everything was being bartered. Decorated animals hobbled along the lake's edge. The village's full life was on display.
Dvij was whisked away by Mahant's men as they approached. Bhavi protested but Dvij waved back - he'd be all right. She had to look after Professor.
Dvij was led to the pandaal accommodating far more people than seemed possible. A procession began, led by Mahant, culminating in distinguished members seated on the dais.

b2-p007.t: Mahant addressed the crowds - future promises, temple construction necessity, garbhadhana importance - shifting success responsibility onto the enfeebled masses...

...rambling predictions, the Wounded One's arrival (pointing sharply at bewildered Dvij),. Professor had somehow gained enough confidence to be placed with distinction on the dais. Long speeches under harsh sun tested endurance.

Theatre began - pandavani, with men` playing both genders, breaking into rhythmic foot-tapping folk dance. Musicians worked away merrily on dhols, pakhawajs, kartals, and taanpuras. The act had a good dose of local wit.

Dvij could not locate Bhavi in the swarm extending to the horizon. For a moment he thought of the dark yogini, then realized she wouldn't dare follow him here. Civilized society was too much risk for a beautiful tribal.

b2-p008.t: Avadhan. That's what this is called. Many people ask questions. Expert has to remember all of them, then respond to each in verses following rules of rasa and alankara.

Next event: 'ask the expert' - numerous people throwing challenging questions at an expert who responded rapidly. The entire interaction in rhyming verse. The expert formed verses at will, tracking all questions.
Techniques of memorization! The entire Vedas handed down orally through millenniums! Students learned forward sequence, backward, skipping syllables - remember it forever!

Most of the crowd dispersed as evening dragged into darkest night. Preparations for the main event continued. Dvij felt increasingly tired, yawning constantly, stretching his eyes to stay open. Bhavi was no longer visible anywhere.
A resounding conch note announced Brahmakaal's arrival. The deity was invited, offered seat, feet washed, sacred water offered for sipping and abhisheka.

b2-p009.t: Resplendent cloth wrapped, garlands draped, incense burned, aarti performed. The ritual began.
Elaborate ritual involved long mantra sequences interspersed with aahutis and aachhmans. Ghee and wood added to the kundli made heat more oppressive than sun.
Every time Dvij lost consciousness, Mahant's conch blare startled him awake.
But Professor was a revelation. No signs of tiredness, hopping about, getting close to pujaris, sliding behind Dvij whispering explanations of each rite.
Land purified, golden kalasha filled with earth, navaratnas, navadhanyas, navakhanijas installed with mantras. The foundation stone placed.

b2-p010.t: By the end, Dvij existed in a plasma state - awake and asleep simultaneously. He didn't remember Professor lifting him up, suffering pins-and-needles in deadwood legs...
...walking past an old musician playing dolefully under thatched extension, or Professor preventing collisions with walls and hedges.
On arrival, Dvij found the first bed already occupied by Bhavi. She stirred, looking up googly-eyed. Professor, on the other hand, was tireless and rushed off to make coffee.
Uncle was strangely active throughout. Where were you? What happened to keeping watch over him?
Never quetion a girl who's not had her beauty sleep.

b2-p011.t: Let's go to his study. He talks most when there.
I've been seeing shadows, hearing sounds. Yesterday I became sure. Bad people are closing in. They know what they want.
I don't fear for you - they won't hurt you. Trust me! I fear for my secret knowledge.
They will strike the lodge. That is inevitable. If I escape alive it will be a boon.
We cannot let it fall in wrong hands. If I'm gone, you must rediscover it.
Yes uncle. But I won't let anything happen to you.
Hush, child! Think of the secret. Resolve to work it out.

b2-p012.t: I will do everything, just as you ask.
Yes, I need to tell her. Oh, this is so thrilling! I've left a clue - a most ingenious clue.
Good! Now I can relax. I know my secret will be safe.
But Professor, you haven't told her what to do.
No uncle! Not another clue! We've not figured out the last one.
Yes - another clue. The toughest - so only those who know me can crack the code.
Ah! The beginning, you ask? I shall tell you.
But I'll say this only once and nothing more. Is that understood?
Look for the knot in the pot.
He sipped the remainder of his coffee, and went out to talk to his trees.

b2-p013.t: Don't ask me. He's your uncle.
Sometimes I wish he made more sense.
That is it? Knot in the pot?
If his clues were simple, they'd be simple for them too.
Our enemies. Those after Professor's secrets.
Our enemies? When did you decide you were on my side?.
Oh come on! Sometimes you treat me a friend, other times a foe. Make up your mind. Do you want me to be with you or not?
Hurt was visible in Dvij's angry eyes. Bhavi momentarily recoiled from the intensity, then stood and turned away deliberately to avoid eye contact.
You cannot be with me until you come clean.
You have to first prove that you are not planted by Mahant to hurt my uncle.

b2-p014.t: Kurup, my uncle's able assistant. Mr. Dvij, the Wounded One with No Past. Glad you managed to run into each other.
Let me do the introductions, boys.
They released each other and a round of apology and handshakes followed. By now Professor had returned, remarking he'd heard a din from his room.
I heard a noise at the door and thought it was an intruder.
I was leaning to push the door open when it suddenly gave way and I fell in.
But if you're his assistant, how come you’re never around?
Professor had sent me up on Dronagiri Parbat few weeks ago. I got back yesterday, rested in a tavern. I have brought this statue he so desired.

b2-p015.t: Did you really bring it? Come on, where is it?
Where is it? I have to feast my eyes on it!
Found it! Here it is, Professor. But its left ear...it is...it is broken.
The statue was indeed sensual art - celestial nymph in asymmetric tribhanga pose, mudras expressing wonderment, ornate alankara showing fine craftsmanship. But the left ear was broken.
Broken? Only two statues of this kind, and you damaged one of them.
I'm not to blame, master. It must have broken when I fell because he pulled the door.
Sorry Professor. I trusted my instincts. There's been too much talk of intruders.
Yes, our nerves are high- strung. Let us rejoice that there is another one which remains intact.
In the ancient temple up the mountain, right next to the spot from where I picked this one.

b2-p016.t: Why do they keep the Gods locked up?"
At night? I guess to keep the thieves out.

They walked toward Sri Mukteshwara temple in the red glow of dusk. The main street looked deserted like a ghost town - doors bolted, windows shuttered against evil spirits. Bhavi rubbed her shoulders against the crisp biting air.
Or the priests do not want people to talk to Gods without their presence.

The scene transformed as the village yawned awake. They walked beneath the tall gopura into a large compound. The temple's steps were wet, recently washed. The majestic layout based on vaastu design - the temple as primordial man.

A pot-bellied attendant confronted them. Question mark eyes perfectly captured his surprise at seeing unexpected strangers. He led them through narrow alleys - the sprawling complex appropriated by Mahant for his confidants.
What are you gaping at...these statues? I hope you know what you are going to do.

Mahant's routine: wake early, ritual bath to wash away sins of the night, meditate, two breakfasts - private with prohibited foods, public without. Private meeting chamber: pillared hall, high ventilators, marble benches, ceiling painted with epic frescos, danseuse sculptures adorning pillars.

b2-p017.t: A thought troubles my mind. What if I am...impure?

Mahant entered with associates - gathered to deter Dvij from doing anything stupid. Sitting on central bench, crossing one leg over other, he chanted a mantra in deep voice. Bhavi felt a shiver at his disparaging look - as if holding her responsible for her uncle's radical thoughts.
Do not burden yourself with trivialities...
...you think I foresaw your arrival but not your faith?
Enough! You are one of us, for I say it is so.
How can someone who has no past know his faith?
But I...who does not know his own name...how do I convince my feeble mind?
Mahant stood almost on his toes, towering over others. His attendants cowered - they'd learned standing during meetings indicated increasing rage.
You have all the answers I seek. I do not understand many things.
Why do we worship idols, for instance?
What is it you do not understand?

The insolent outsider raised tough questions - free thinking and scientific enterprise, education of masses and removal of superstition, abolishing inhuman practices and bringing inclusivity in society - everything under the sun that he wholeheartedly abhorred.

The fuming Mahant found excuse to end this conversation, which had not gone at all as he would have liked. It was time to initiate morning temple services. Before exiting, he advised Dvij to remain in the temple, and even more threatingly, advised Bhavi to not do so.

b2-p018.t: Mahant has installed goons at all the exits. There's no way I can get out. You leave while you can.
My plan was to push him...to get him to make a mistake.
That was your plan? To rankle Mahant.

They followed the priests behind Mahant. In the compound, an elephant's mahavat wiped its thick skin with a large sponge. Dvij saw Mahant motion to men who dispersed, showing up at the gopuras - exits blocked.
Shouldn't you be worried about your uncle instead?

Just then the temple bells started pealing, causing everyone to stop in their tracks. A loud commotion could be heard outside the east gopura. Dvij climbed steps to observe. Mahant stood a couple steps above and behind him. People rushed toward the entrance from all directions.

b2-p019.t: Object of displeasure: a mendicant dressed in tatters, making lewd gestures toward passersby. Someone threw a stone. Mob sprang into action. The mendicant continued his wild ways. Dvij recalled tantric baba's discourse on the three stages of renunciation followed by Shaivites.
Why, O pious Mahant, do you not throw stones at that man? He seeks hatred in his path to salvation. He has come to your doorstep, and being a man of religion, you must not deny him.
I am Mahant. My virtues are accepted on my word. Question them and you question your own existence.
I order you to go forward and stop that man from being hurt by the stones, for you are the saviour.
Dvij realized Mahant had thrust him into controlling a mob spiraling out of control. He stepped into the crowd, Mahant's men flanking his sides.

His presence had immediate effect - but entirely different from what Mahant expected. The crowd's interest in the mendicant dropped instantly, shifting to Dvij. They moved toward him with outstretched hands, like zombies, stumbling over each other, trying to reach him, touch him.

b2-p020.t: That old woman. I think they are saying she is healed.
The one with leprosy. They think it was because she had touched you.
Look at all these hands! Help me out of here!
They cannot touch me. Hold on to my hand.
If I could find out which one is yours.

Somehow he managed to grab her hand in the melee of hands engulfing him. He felt a tug, a jerk, and a pull, and his feet began finding space to move. He held on to the hand as he willingly let himself be pulled.

Through a sea of limbs jostling for space, over men prostrate in reverence, from between those clamoring for his healing touch. Lo and behold, they were out of the crowds! A mad scramble saw them manage to create distance between themselves and the chasing crowd.
After a quick burst through the narrow streets lined with tin shops with corrugated iron tops, most of the crowd had stalled the chase, leaving only Mahant's men in hot pursuit.

b2-p021.t: A rapid sprint brought them to the external wall of fort ruins. Exertion had taken its toll - panting heavily, stopping occasionally to steady beating hearts. Bhavi pointed to a path beyond the wall curving upward. They moved at brisk pace.
Keep going! We’re not there yet.
But they will follow us in this shelter!

The path opened into a plateau flanked by a humongous boulder on one side and a low-lying structure on the other. Bhavi quickly moved inside - essentially a roof of slabs supported by narrow pillars, probably serving as shelter for passing hermits.
Suddenly Bhavi put brakes on her run - so abrupt Dvij almost ran into her.
This is the entrnace to Bhoodara caves. They are a chakravyuha inside the belly of the earth.
Nnobody who has entered has made it back.
That does it. I’m going in.

b2-p022.t: Watch your step. The floor is uneven.
And watch the ceiling. It drops sharply at places
And you watch your language. This was the abode of a hermit during the reign of Shakalaya clan.

At one point the ceiling came so low they had to crawl on all fours. At another, walls were so close together they tucked in stomachs to walk through jutting rocks. Air turned dank from moisture that had never evaporated.
I'll switch off the light. They'll be too scared to follow us this deep but you never know.

They reached the hermit’s sleeping place - there was a flat stone bed with a niche meant for keeping a diya beside it. Bhavi sat down and massaged her hurting feet. They could hear feeble echoes of confused voices coming from rooms above them.

b2-p023.t: What do you think they will do if they catch us?
Keep me locked up. He wants full control over my actions and I have not been playing along.
What I wonder is why has Mahant not used you as a bait to get to uncle’s secret. There must be a reason.
He was a Goswami, highly revered. He used to live in a math inside the fort. When the fort fell, the sage gave everything up and decided to spend the rest of his life in isolation.
Though never seen again, legend goes he will arise when the fort, and the math inside it, are restored to their former glory.
Great! We’ve managed to trap ourselves in an escapable cave system.. What do you propose to do next?
Let’s wait for some time to make sure those goons have left.
We get up and walk out.

b2-p024.t: Oh right! We simply get up and walk out, right?
I will hit you. If it was that simple, someone would have done it.
I know how to retrace our steps.
What makes you think I will.

Up and around they crawled through the rooms, Dvij seeming to know exactly which cave to move to next. It was a matter of time before streaks of sunlight streaming in from the cave's entrance brought out a mix of relief and disbelief on Bhavi's face.

b2-p025.t: A simple matter of using my memory.
Wasn't that the one thing you were not good at...remembering things?
You saw the avadhan show at the ceremony?
Professor explained their memorization technique to me. I tried it on a shloka and it worked.
This shloka gave you some magical powers?
No, but it did help me remember the value of pi.
You have no idea what you are saying, do you?

b2-p026.t: Amazing! But how did that help us?
So youcounted the number of exits following the sequence of the value of pi
No miracle. Nature, human intellect and the unknown.
One good thing is Mahant will think we are lost forver.
Reminds me. Why were people saying that old woman is cured?
No, I meant it's a miracle that I'm standing in the sun and not worried about my complexion.
The water I gave her to drink.
Viruses that kill leprosy germs. That’s what healed her.
But why are people not getting healed by bathing in Sheetal lake?
I got the water from upstream. It must be getting contaminated downstream..
We don't know yet. Answer is in the unknown.

b2-p027.t: What predator could be lurking there?
They do that when they sense danger.
The birds are unusually chirpy today.

The lodge should have been swathed in mid-afternoon stillness when winds die and trees grow quiet. But today was different. Bitter bird chattering came from the lodge's direction from quite a distance.
I don’t have a good feeling about this.
Don’t we keep the gate latched?
Someone's back could be seen flitting through the trees. Dvij gave quick chase but the suspect was lost in the wilderness. He ran around the building to the study.
Bhavi was standing outside the study door that opened outwards. She was in a state of shock. Inside, Professor was bent forward over the board game displaying a most unnatural form of surrender.
He’s alive. You need to take over.

Dvij saw a deep gash at the back of Professor's head. He tried to lift it but it rolled back listlessly. He removed the crushed glasses, tucked his arms under Professor's shoulders and dragged him to the couch.

b2-p028.t: Bhavi sprang into action. She brought her medicine bag from her room, quickly scanned the damage to his skull, and applied the necessary antiseptic and bandages.
I am administering a dosage intravenously. He should come around soon.
It’s a contusion, yes. Fortunately, not too deep. He’s unconscious from the shock.

Kurup was in the room by the time Dvij returned with the pillows, watching over Bhavi as she administered an injection. Bhavi asked him to lift Professor's legs and Dvij to insert the pillows under them.
In the shed, trying to fix the statue you broke. I saw someone running away so ran behind him.
You say you were running. I know I was running. Problem is: I saw only 2 people running.

b2-p029.t: What are you saying? That I hurt the master and ran away?
More importantly: did they find it. I’ll check the bookshelves if anything is missing.
Stop arguing. Whoever came here was after something. Question is: what was it?
I’ll look into his papers. Kurup - you check the shelves for missing statues or rocks.
Only think missing on the shelves is the statue I am fixing.
Nothing amiss on the bookshelves either. They are as disorganized as always.
Wait a minute! Wasn't there something on uncle's desk when we left him this morning?
The big black book! It's gone.

b2-p030.t: This Kurup...his face...what happened to him?
He’s been doing odd jobs for uncle ever since.
A tiger. The beast tore open his face. He is lucky to have survived.
It's funny how a crook sees a crook in everybody else.
I take it that he’s trustworthy.
Uncle had asked us to look for the knot in the pot if something happened to him.
Could he have meant Lord Ganesha?
It can’t be actual pots. That’s too literal.
We should look at it as a symbol. Like kumbha...the fertility pot...symbolic of the womb.
I recall seeing something in a book...this one...

b2-p031.t: Let me turn the pages. Oh, here. Shrivatsa - the endless knot.
Yes! Kalasha - the pot used in religious ceremonies.
Then the knot would also be symbolic of something.
The image is symbolic of Vishnu, the tuft of hair on his chest. It also symbolizes union of two opposing forces - wisdom and compassion.
So if we find the kalasha, we look for this symbol and we would have our hands on my uncle's secret.
There must be a kalasha in every hut in the village. How do we find the one we're looking for?
It cannot be just any kalasha. It has to be significant. Like the one on top of Mahant’s temple.
How would uncle reach its top?
Not unless he saw what was being put into it at the time of installation on the top of vimana.
That's true. He would not know what's in that kalasha.
That's it! You are a genius, Bhavi. You solved the puzzle.
Did I? I must have, for you seem so sure about it.

b2-p032.t: Put it another way – Prof would have been able to tinker with only that kalasha whose installation ceremony he attended.
You sure did. You said Prof could not have reached the kalasha other than at the time when it was being installed. Right?
It can. There are two kalashas in a temple. One above the vimana, the other, right below the garbhagriha.
Do you recall any recent ceremony that your uncle attended?
Why yes! The garbhadhana ceremony. But how can it have a kalasha when the temple itself is yet to be constructed?
A kalasha expresses the idea of filling the void. An auspicious vessel. No ceremony can be performed without its installation.
That must be it. The ceremony was about installing the kalasha which stands for the garbha. That would explain why uncle was so so desperate to attend it.
It would also explain his agitated state. He must have had foreboding of danger. Maybe one shadow too many.
So uncle decides to act fast. He thinks hard and comes up with a plan. He makes sure to attend the garbhadhana ceremony...
...and slip something in the kalasha before it's lowered into its chamber. It must have been something he valued highly.
What do you think it could be?
No idea. All I know is that it is marked with an endless knot.

b2-p033.t: "Later that night, two silhouettes slipped out into the darkness. A gibbous moon cast enough light to keep them from running into things. They moved at a brisk pace.
As Dvij had predicted, there was nobody around. The aadharshila moved with some effort.

Light from Dvij's cell illuminated the objects residing on the thick layer of sand. There were the navratnas, nine mounds of grains, and nine pieces of wrapped parchment, all neatly arranged in a 3x3 grid. All but one had mantras written inside. The only exception was the one with a tiny knot drawn on it.

Bhavi grabbed that piece of parchment and nodded to Dvij who switched off the light, replaced the kalasha's lid and moved the aadharshila back to its proper place. The two silhouettes slipped back as surreptitiously as they had come.

Back in the lodge, two pairs of eyes under the glare of the study lamp stared at the unwrapped piece of parchment for a long, long time. The parchment was crumpled with intersecting creases. It had a number of line drawings etched onto it, slightly smudged, that could not have made sense to anybody.

b2-p034.t: Dvij lifted the paper in front of the light bulb to see if any text was hidden anywhere, but that exercise was futile. He expressed his disappointment with an audible sigh that fluttered the paper under the desk. Bhavi gave him an angry look, pulled out the paper and kept it firmly back in front of them.
It's a crazy jumble of symbols.
Uncle is unconscious and you’r making stupid jokes?
I'm sorry. But none of this makes any sense at all.
Sleep over it. We will work on it tomorrow.

Dvij did just that, and as soon as he did, slumber caught up with him. He was sleeping before he knew it, his dream being an incessant torrent of tormenting symbols. Bhavi, on the other hand, was determined to continue working.

b3-p001.t: You’ve got a stiff neck from sleeping on the parchment.

Next morning, Dvij shrugged Bhavi's shoulder gently. She woke with a start, straightened her back with a jerk and looked confused. She tried to turn her head then gave out with a groan, massaging the side of her neck.
...but he’s still unconscious. That’s not good.
Don’t worry. He’ll come around soon enough.
Bhavi smiled weakly, still struggling with pain that radiated from neck muscles. Then, as her mind played back events of previous evening, she recalled the fate that had befallen her beloved uncle.
What? Never saw a girl with crinkled cheek?
Not that. I am checking if any of the symbols got transcripted onto your face.
Oh! I remember. I turned it upside down in frustration.

b3-p002.t: Good! Who knows what your makeup would have done to the sumbols.
So that each of us can work on it. Here’s yours...
No need to worry. I made three copies of it.
Your team. One of them is a flunky with a half-eaten face. The other does not even know his own name.

Dvij folded the paper Bhavi handed him and tucked it somewhere carelessly. Bhavi viewed the act with disapproval. Dvij acted as if he had picked up the parchment and folded it into an imaginary plane and launched it into flight.

Bhavi shared one of the copies with Kurup. She gave background about a secret her uncle possessed and that they have to solve the puzzles. The conversation went in all directions, but by the end Kurup seemed to have understood most of it.
I was hoping you will not ask that.
I think I know where to start.

b3-p003.t: I am serious. Remember prof has left clues in the valley. What had he asked us?
Oh, you do? And where exactly?
I think it was that...we ask for directions.
I don’t know. You tell us.
I give up! Who do we ask?
Why, the cardinal lords! The Gods who preside over directions. Like Kubera for north.

'Remember the pasha at the fort temple? Which lord has pasha?' 'Varuna!' 'And he presides over west.' Bhavi found the temple location. 'Why, that is west!'. 'That is why we found the pasha in the temple at the fort. It IS one of the clues scattered by Professor in the valley.'

b3-p004.t: The humble cook had entered, hands busy dusting off dry atta from his palms, intending to inform them breakfast parathas were ready. However, he was gently persuaded by Bhavi to allow them more time before they could break their overnight fast. Maharaj grumbled his way out of the room.
These eight symbols of weapons are spread out in eight directions of the valley. We need to find out the exact spots. Lots of legwork.
I saw some of those symbols when we scanned the valley earlier and had captured them.
I may be able to help again.
Why, I do. I’m not using it as there’s no connectivity. But wait! How will we upload pictures from your phone?
Would you believe it? There's a USB chord in the camera bag that I found in my car. I'll fetch it while you set up your laptop.
This is no use. If only we had a computer.

b3-p005.t: By the time Dvij returned, Bhavi had set up her laptop. He plugged in the charger into a multiplug and the data chord onto the laptop's port. The operating system automatically installed the required drivers and progressively the images got uploaded to a folder Bhavi had created.
After an hour of stopping and starting the slideshow, zooming and panning images, selecting and saving photos, the group arrived at conclusion they had all but 2 symbols identified.

It was decided Kurup would head out to search for ankusha and Dvij for shakti. When the two menfolk had left, she asked still grumbling Maharaj to serve breakfast in the room itself. Bhavi had lost all sense of time when they returned.
That’s a bummer. How do we fill the gap?
I have tried every possible way to arrange them. Problem is we have 8 pictures and we're trying to position them in a 3x3 grid.

b3-p006.t: I think Professor had said something else. Even more cryptic.
Yes, I remember. Uncle had said ‘ask for directions to indescribable wealth’. Now what could that mean?
I think the number ‘8’ is somehow significant.
At least I am coming up with something. What are you doing?
Sorry! I’m only trying to encourage you to come up with more ideas..
How about the ashtalakshmis? The eight goddesses.

b3-p007.t: The gap is gone. This might just work.

When the ideas did not work. Bhavi went to work on the images. Her aim was to somehow fill the gap created when trying to position 8 images in a 3x3 grid. Her solution was to overlay two translucent layers of 4 images each - top one for the mahadikpalas and the other for the rest.
Prof would have pictured those buildings to fit into a larger picture.
That’s it! Something needs to be taking shape.
I wonder we have to zoom in and out to line up the edges of the objects.

Bhavi busied herself zooming pictures in and out, trying to align lines - a vertical pipe running through the tavern transitioning into a boundary wall of a house on the hill. A distinct shape was beginning to emerge but difficult to pick out from amidst the clutter of distracting shapes and colours.
This could be the facade of some building.
You would not have to tilt your heads if you did not tilt those pictures in the first place.

b3-p008.t: It's like those magic pictures I had a book of when I was a child.But if you looked right through it, look far away into infinity, a shape would start steeping out through those crazy patterns.
It looks somewhat like the backside of a building. See the line there...it could be a roof.
Autostereograms! One needs to go wall-eyed to see the hidden image. Isn't it strange that I know what they are called but I don't know if I ever saw one?

Features emerged through collaboration: 'That dark line going vertically...a pipe. This brownish patch at bottom middle...a door.' 'That looks like a cubist door. Part of the wall covered by tree canopy. Even a suggestion of a ladder.' 'Yes, a wall. Too ugly to be a facade. Must be a backside, rather nondescript.’
I’m telling you...I have seen this wall somewhere.
That can only mean one thing...

b3-p009.t: They rushed through the illuminated courtyard and by the side of the kitchen (much to Maharaj's surprise) onto the narrow backyard. When the others caught up, they found Dvij straining his neck looking up at the backside.
If this is the wall, there should have been a tree here.
There used to be one here, right outside the perimeter.
The tree was brought down during last winter season, most likely by poor peasants who needed firewood to keep warm. Winter was terribly cold.
Let’s circle around the house and climb that mound to get a view.
What’s that green patch up there?

b3-p010.t: I do know something that can help us - Master's leaf collection!
That’s correct! Uncle has a folder that describes all kinds of leaves.
Then what are we waiting for? Let’s go!
There was yet another mad scramble, this time not involving the kitchen (thus leaving Maharaj at peace with his stoking).

Kurup pulled out a handmade scrapbook. Leaves were pressed between pairs of transparencies glued together. Leaves on left with descriptions on right - colloquial names, scientific names, and description of their lamina (the shape in outline).
With these four parameters we could describe any leaf fairly distinguishingly.

b3-p011.t: I need you guys to fetch me an accurate copy.
Both of you have to go. Two pairs of eyes are better than one.
It’s a bit blurred. Hopefully Kurup’s will be clearer.
Meanwhile why don’t we check out it’s lacuna?
Yes, a gap in my understanding.
Lamina! Lacuna is a gap, silly.
It is spatulate (spoon- shaped, that is), with a spiny margin near the acute tip but smooth otherwise.
Here's what our mystery leaf looks like...
I’ll create copies. Let us compare against the transparencies.

Next two hours were spent slogging through transparencies, periodically punctuated by calls to Maharaj for tea. But the exercise only resulted in a sequence of unfaltering rejections. At the end, they were left with nothing.

b3-p012.t: It means Prof was smart enough not to document the secret plant in this leaf collection. It must be in the black book, which is gone.
That’s terrible! We’ll never find out the identity of this leaf.
I have sren him scribble notes. They are in this drawer.

What they saw were fragments of ancient texts surrounded by an intricate web of comments, juxtaposed with plethora of illustrations, sufficient to dissuade the most determined minds. Kurup divided them into three stacks.
I’m not giving up. I’m hoping you will find the answer.

b3-p013.t: Have you gone crazy? You pick each one of them.
What are you guys looking at? Is this some trick?
But Dvij was seriously engaged in the paper that had landed on top, and very shortly Kurup had joined him. Bhavi, arms akimbo, remained unimpressed.
Have a look yourself and decide.
Something a lot more potent than tea.
Some? Are you thinking uncle found the original soma plant?
Do you recall what he had said when he explain the soma pavanama process?
Bah! Mere speculation. I may or I may not. If you want to know my secret you will have to discover it yourself.
I wonder, Professor, maybe you found that original species...is that your secret?

The soma pavamana clarification process: washing stems, crushing in mortar, filtering through sheepskin, diluting with milk. The cosmic recreation: mills as thunder, filter as clouds, juice as masculine seed in rain, mixing with milk as feminine coupling creating cosmos.

b3-p014.t: If I was Mahant I would do anything to know the secret of the elusive Soma plant. After all, an entire mandala of Rig Veda is devoted to extolling the Lord that presides over this precious plant.
Why, Sushruta talks about 24 different kinds of soma plants that grow on mountains.
Many claim soma is some psychoactive mushroom, but Rig Veda describes it as a leafy plant with long tawny stalks, which grows around water bodies.
It would be a priceless discovery. But how do you think uncle did it?
You only said he spent time with the tribals. He could have got hold of documents preserved over centuries.
There are secret societies that protect esoteric texts from falling into wrong hands.
Even Emperor Ashoka is said to have 9 navratnas, believed to be immortals protecting specialized knowledge.
Maybe the custodians are protecting the knowledge of how the 33 Gods of Rig Veda became the 33 kotis of Gods in our pantheon.
Nowadays, all it takes to find knowledge is to search the net.
Maybe the secret works explain how the cosmogony of hiranya garbha corroborates with the belief that the cosmos is a work of Vishvakarma, himself a son of Lord Brahma.

b3-p015.t: I don't think uncle meant for us to look for soma plant even if he did find out about it.
Because it's just not him. He may have challenged beliefs but he had a sincere appreciation of religion.
Mahant would see this as a source of wealth and would go to any extent to possess it.
I don't see soma fitting into his scheme of things.
I’ve tasted the modern version made with substitute plants, and can only imagine what the drink of the gods must have tasted like.
Why, I’d kill just to taste it.
Disgusting! Anyways, there are other things which if discovered would allow Mahant to amass wealth.
Such as...he could sell the sculptures scattered around the hills. He's got a right- turning conch, I have heard.
Points accepted. But how do any of them relate to a leaf?
That's right, he has a dakshinavarti shankh. He even has a large shaligram shila.

b3-p016.t: Counterpoint accepted. But maybe we don’t take the leaf literally? Maybe it’s a symbol.
Leaf is a symbol of what? Where does this leave us?
This leaves us with our backs pressed...to the back wall.
Let us ponder over Prof’s parchment, all over again.

For the next hour, the study possessed a silence reserved for libraries. An occasional sigh of dismay, a false exclamation, a cough to clear a cluttered mind, and tuneful whistle that faded away almost as soon as it started were the only sound heard above the gentle whirring of the overhead fan.
Ol' Prof is a genius to visualize how those different buildings would form the shape of the lodge's back wall when positioned in two overlapping squares.
I am going to wring your neck!
Is that what you have been thinking all this while? What about the parchment?
Oh that! I cracked it a long time ago.

b3-p017.t: A confession: when I said I have solved the puzzle, what I meant was that I have an appeoach to solving it.
I was lying there just a few days ago.

Next morning, they had Professor to the convalescence room which had been occupied by a comatose Dvij earlier. The room was airier, with space to enough fit the party of three along with Maharaj who sat cross-legged at the foot of the bed.
All codes need a key to crack. Now who created this parchment?
I saw a thought-process so extraordinary, so radical that I do see how he could possess secret knowledge and why he felt vulnerable.
Then Professor is the key to cracking it. We need to reconstruct his thoughts.
And how do we do that?
Each of us share our thoughts about him. Three vantage points. I knew him least so let me go go first.
Who, me? I will forever remain indebted to master. My own people hated me after my skirmish with the tiger.
I used to hide deep inside the forests to escape the torture. It was at a time like this when master saw value in my meaningless escapades.
He obviously spent his lifetime in pursuit of the hidden. He loved images, and longed to understand them.
I brought all kinds of objects for him from forests and hills. He seemed to be able to read them, much like his books.
Normal day-to-day things appear different to him. Everything is symbolic of some truth that is hidden from the rest of us.
Books! Uncle always loved his books. But not more than he loves me. His intellect is immense, but he is equally humble,

b3-p018.t: What’s wrong? Why did you start pacing the room?
What is it? What are you thinking of?
I’m thinking of the one common theme in all our descriptions. I called them images, Kurup called them objects and you called them things. Do you realize what they are? Icons!
Iconography! Study of symbols in socio-religious context. That's what these are... on the parchment... symbols waiting to be deciphered.
The symbols represent abstract concepts. His books, his papers, his gibberish notes... all of them will help us decode the secret.
What do you see on the parchment?
Strange, yes. But not scattered. Look carefully... the shapes are arranged in rows.
It means that each row is a puzzle. 5 puzzles means 5 solutions.
They do look lined up. But what does it mean?
You’re saying each row will have to be solved separately?
Yes. And solving a row is a lot simpler than having to solve the whole parchment.
The first message is just this symbol?

b3-p019.t: No worries. I have solved it.
Yes, as that's the only image in the first row.
Even this does not make any sense to me.
Oh, did you? And what’s the secret message?
That's very interesting, but there's just one small problem.
Yes, Gyaneshwar. Whatever it is we are looking for we will find in the Gyaneshwar temple.
The valley has 108 temples but not one dedicated to Lord Gyaneshwar?
There is no Gyaneshwar temple in the valley.
It’s quite simple. The vertical eye is a recognizable symbol for Lord Shiva.
And Gyaneshwar is Lord Shiva in deep meditation under the Kalpataru tree. So vertical eye in tree is...
How did you arrive at Gyaneshwar from this tree-with-an- eye image?

b3-p020.t: Oh that? I thought you got it too because Lord Shiva is also known as Neelkanth.
Neel kanth...that could happen if you wring someone's neck.
All this is fine, but there’s still the problem that there is no Gyaneshwar temple.
That’s true. But he may be partly right. That vertical eye can only mean Lord Shiva.
The most important of his form-temples in this valley is the Kaal Bhairava.
I think it is time for us to pay that tantalizing tantric a visit.

They immediately took off. Yogini appeared as mysteriously as she had disappeared. She was mute for most of the journey but became agitated as they approached the tantric's abode, circling around them uttering fierce words in her tribal language.
Why do I get a feeling she's trying to stop us from going into the Aghori ashram?
Maybe she thinks we are here to return her. I bet she's not going to follow us inside.

b3-p021.t: The late afternoon sun formed a harsh reflection off the still surface of the lake. The reflected light glinted off polished stone surfaces making it difficult to study the external structure. Inside, diffused light formed subdued patterns easier on the eye.
See the eye on the shivalinga in the garbhagriha? That’s the eye we are looking for.

Peace reigned inside. A half-dozing priest sat by the daan-paatra. Friezes, mouldings, celestial dancers all continued their dance to lores of millenniums past. Polished pillars, garlanded deities, some flanked by fearsome beasts, adorned niches big and small.
Let’s look around. Shouldn’t be that hard to find.
"The ashram is full of pipal trees. There is one large fig banyan tree under whose aerial roots sadhus sit in contemplation. But none is close enough
The friezes are full of trees, but I don't think that is what are looking for.

b3-p022.t: We're looking at it all wrong. Each part of puzzle is symbolic, like this beast.
I recall a discussion with ol’ Prof about Vaastu. He had compared the vertical structure of a temple to a tree.
The underground kalasha is the roots. Structure above the aadharshila is likened to the visible portion of the tree.

The ceiling above the garbhagriha is called kapotha which literally translates to 'where doves sit' - signifying the branches. Thus the garbhagriha is the trunk. The whole of the temple...it is a tree!
The image on the parchment had the eye in the trunk. That is the eye on the linga in the garbhagriha. What does it see?
That’s the third eye of Lord Shiva. It sees everything.
The hole is visible only from the garbhagriha.
No, something specific. From a hole in the ceiling somewhere up there.

b3-p023.t: So you are saying that the eye is looking at the dhwajastambha?

The garbhagriha idol is installed such that its line of sight is directed at the dhwajastambha - the tall pole for lighting diyas - in front of the eastern rajagopura. The mantapa ceiling has a hole in the line of sight.
That...we can know only when we step out on the front porch.

From behind the large monolithic Nandi next to the balipeetha stood a tall pole with miniature arms for mounting diyas. Beyond it stood a resplendent gopura. Further beyond stood the mighty Dronagiri Parvat.
That is where we will find our elusive plant.

b3-p024.t: Master found oil! Just look at the middle circle!
We have to find a message from all the symbols together.
Maybe they are 3 sudarshan chakras. That’s Lord Vishnu!
That’s Lord Shiva symbol. Together they mean Lord Harihara!
There’s no petrol in the tank. How will you drive it?
Can we take your scooter for a spin?
There, leaning against a sack in the dusty yard, was Bhavi's faded pink scooter — dormant for ages, and yet...
Dvij tilted the tank. Then he siphoned petrol from his own car. Then, with a throttle and a roar — the dormant machine sprang back to life.

b3-p025.t: They negotiated hilly curves, drove through marshy stretches, and into a grove...
...stirring up, like a hornet's nest, a bevy of shepherding boys.
Let’s head back. I think I know how to solve the puzzle.
The Sudarshan Chakra is symbolic of Kaal Purusha — the celestial man of time. The nakshatras are the moon's 27 wives.

b3-p026.t: Ok, ok! We all know what yoni means.
The flute is Dhanishta, ruled by Mars. The teardropis Aridra, ruled by Rahu. And what we thought was a key is a yoni — the symbol of Bharani, ruled by Venus.
The complement to linga — the piece that completes—
All I know is the pundits use nakshatras to advise the name of a child. My own sacral name is...
You have anything more sensible to say?
Of course it is. Gotilal is my given name.
The name will bring you success in chaupad.
Not you Kurup. The coded message...it spells out a name.
We will get a name from the combination of the 3 columns.

b3-p027.t: A cloak of darkness surrounded them as they circled the village. Ponga was found at the forest's edge, talking to anything that cast a shadow. Kurup squats under a peepal tree, then — registering where he is — immediately stands up and moves away briskly.
His mind may not understand us, but his stomach understands hunger.
What I don’t get is what will we do with him?
I believe he knows something. His mind is like a little lost machine that will activate when a trigger condition is reached.

The procession walked back to the lodge — Kurup dangling the last roti, Ponga shuffling, Dvij's feet still moving forward even as his eyes were on the mountain, as if asking "Could it be that this mountain that holds the key to my past?".

b3-p028.t: You’re not actually planning to go up Dronagiri Parbat. That’s thousands of feet high.
I, for one, will go for that achar.
We’ll go for a hike up the mountain.
Uncle’s still not woken up. He might be in a coma.
Power had gone out half the day ago. Maharaj relit the fire. They ate by the angeethi's shifting light — Ponga settling, as always, for an onion and his rotis.
We have to go before Mahant does.

The motley crew — Dvij's mock-formal announcement. The hard yellow unshaded bulb back on. Dvij moved to the centre of the room, one arm raised as if addressing troops, his expression theatrical gravity.
A small cooking pot — absolutely essential. One has to be prepared to live off the land.
Or one may desire a decent cup of coffee.
And I will not go without my medical kit.
The equipment was assembled on the study table. Ropes. Knives. Candles. Kurup's pot. Bhavi's medical kit. One sleeping bag — provenance unclear.

b3-p029.t: I’m worried about Mahant. For all we know...
...he might have someone keeping a watch on us right this moment..
Sheesh! You scared me. What happened?
Oh — nothing. Just the draft. It gave me the chills.
Dvij noticed that all windows and doors were shuttered. The question of a draft did not arise.
I know what you find so funny. My team, isn’t it?
Just look at us. You can either laugh of cry...take you pick.
Hmph! Either way, we are taking a hike tomorrow.
Sleep well. We start first thing tomorrow morning.
Bhavi switched off the light. Kurup walked to the shed. Dvij stepped out onto the gravel path. The last bulb went dark. The mountain waited.

b3-p030.t: The iron gate creaked. Yogini was tense — the night holding its breath around her. When their eyes met, the vibes were those of gentility — her eyes beseeching affection, his revealing a want to extend company to her lonely self. He extended his hand. She accepted it.
It was Bhavi — half behind the curtain, her face devoid of all emotion. She looked in their direction for some time. Then she turned and walked away.
He talked for a long time to someone who understood none of it — and meant every word.
Whew! I don’t think I could have said all that to someone who understood what I was saying.
Across the courtyard, Ponga had discovered the joy of sleeping on a full stomach.

b3-p031.t: Kurup — shed. Ponga — floor. Yogini — his room. All accounted for. All asleep. All except the sliver of gold beneath Bhavi's door. He knocked quietly. A slight push revealed the doors to be open.

Bhavi lay half-reclining on a rolling bolster, staring into nothingness. She turned away when she became aware of him, at the edge of her vision. He found a chair near the door and made himself as small as possible.
What do you think you are doing?
Who else do you see in this room?
How does one suggest that to someone who does not understand your language?
She was freezing out on the cold pavement, that poor girl. I merely... suggested she sleep in my bed.

b3-p032.t: It’ll be better if you don’t say anything.
Yogini is what Prof would call 'an immaculate incarnation of Tripura Sundari.' Any man in his right mind would find her attractive. And so I did.
What followed was the proverbial pause when nobody knows what to do next. Both stood rooted at their spots, moving their hands clumsily, unsure of what to do with them.
Are you going to apologize or not?
But you asked me not to say anything.
I didn’t say you couldn’t apologize.
Not that I care. Why should I?
He wisely let that pass, and busied himself scratching the calluses formed by long walks in Professor's aged wooden padukas.

b3-p033.t: I was thinking about things you have said... your memory loss... not being Mahant's associate... all of it.
Did you mean what you said? That you felt pity for that girl? And nothing else?
Yes, that is all I felt for her.
I don’t find myself willing to believe any of them.
It’s amavasya - a new moon takes birth tonight. It’s the night of seeking spiritual liberation..
Night has a way of seducing you back into its womb.
They had walked out without noticing—through the grumbling gravel path, past the creaking gate—too engrossed in themselves to care for the world.
You see that? That’s the main temple. Mahant's party —going out to search for the same thing as we are. Just as we thought.
