b3-p034.t: They also say that travel on the first day of the new moon can end only in calamity.
Then it will be as much a disaster for Mahant as for us.
Bhoots, prets prey on unsuspecting souls, not forlorn ones.
Look at that. The universe has enough space for a trillion stars, but not for one man's ambition.
That’s a peepal tree you’re sitting under.
The valley pulsates with suffering. I am supposed to be their saviour. How do I save those who do not wish to be saved?
In total darkness we stop seeing with our eyes. It's then that the mind's eye opens—the omniscient third eye. To experience the absolute, we need our senses shut down. Absolutely completely.
I am at the kundalini's base... at the muladhara. The base of a bottomless pit.
I wish I could be that Sarathi that Lord Krishna was to his Partha. But uncle chose you.
Don't worry. Come tomorrow morning and you’ll find yourself rising above all this vapidity.
Bhavi had meant the trek they were to undertake in a few hours. She did not realize how important those few words would become for the deeply dejected Dvij.

b4-p001.t: Everyone was caught equally unprepared next morning, They prayed to the array of Gods..
...gorged on tumblers of milk and paranthas cooked in ghee...
...instructed Maharaj to care for the peacefully sleeping Professor, and bid an emotional farewell to the dilapidated lodge.
Fear not. Lord Pushan is with us.
Rest of journey is on foot. Stick to the group.

The first leg: a bullock-cart, Kurup's idea from his night in the cowshed. It moved northward through the valley fringes, hidden by dense foliage. There being no road beneath them, remaining aboard required holding each other from falling off.

b4-p002.t: The group moved fast, led by the nimble Kurup. Their only delays: the constant pit stops for the tottering Ponga to catch up. Bhavi was more conscious of the attention Yogini paid to Dvij—unconvinced he was as unaffected as he appeared.
Abruptly the trees ended. Mount Dronagiri rose sharply toward the wide blue sky—like a cinemascope screen seen from the front row. Everyone tilted their heads upward. Everyone, that is, except Kurup.
Kurup patted at the grassy areas—he had seen peasants lose cattle to the devouring sinkholes. He found the tribal trail, hidden under the overgrown grass, and gave strict instruction: stay within it.

At the other end: a pushkarini flanked by a small white mandir with a vermillion Lord Hanuman. Grey langurs chattered mildly in nearby trees. The pond was muddy and filled with pinkish lotus petals flowering on floating fronds.

b4-p003.t: I am sure Prof likes this spot.
Open spaces. Prof loves them as much as I am scared of them.
Yes, he used to come here often. But how did you know?
Like the flag on Arjuna's chariot! This lodge is that chariot and I am Parthasarathi. I wait for a deserving Arjuna to appear.
Oh where could you be, my deserving Partha?
Centuraies of submissiveness have made us lose our will to question.
Aha! You are inquisitive. I like that.

b4-p004.t: No, I meant... where is this valley?
This valley...it could be anywhere. And yet, it is nowhere.
Their mesolithic red-and-green paintings survive to this day in the depths of the Bhoodara cave system, over yonder.
Nobody knows when the earliest inhabitants came to the valley. They inhabited the forest fringes—fierce fighters, hunters in groups.
You would not believe what the texts say about ashvamedha yagya.
I have found evidence of the Bahlika culture in this very valley.
They ate beef with garlic and drank an intoxicant called gauda.
Charvaka's texts were not destroyed. I have discovered some in this very valley
So you see... this valley is a microsorm of the entire universe.
And now... I must find solace. Solace! Solace!

b4-p005.t: To get to the base, we have to cross Himapan forest — home of the violent Nagas.

The vantage point — pushkarini behind them, Mount Dronagiri looming ahead. The south-east face jagged; the north-west face a gradual green slope — the better hiking route. The Himapan forest between them and the mountain's north-west base.
Forest has a beast even Nagas fear.
Tiger. This is the same forest where a tiger did this to me.
The edge of a bamboo grove where Ponga attends to himself. The forest beyond — dark, dense, the realm of the Nagas.
We cannot risk going into the forest.
I guess we walk around it.
Too risky... Mahant’s men will spot us.
Can’t you get her to leave? Same as how you got her into your bed. With gestures & motions.
We can't move fast enough with him...
...and we can't go slowly for fear of being seen with her.

b4-p006.t: Almost on cue, Yogini gathered herself up and started walking. Equally instantaneously, Ponga stopped fiddling with himself and followed — his tottering frame supported by a partly-chewed bamboo hiking pole.
How curious. She has a free will.
No — it can't be. Are they really going where I think they are going?
And where does he think he is off to?
They are going into the forest! That is suicide!!

There come moments when everyone is equally undecided on what to do next. This was one of them. A series of events gave them the belief that they had decided to move forward — and very quickly they had caught up with the unlikeliest of pairs.

b4-p007.t: Then we should wear masks like this one.
We do not have time to make so many of them.
Why don’t we strap our backs together?
Ever tried running like that? With a tiger chasing?
It's a mask — for the tiger. Tigers hunt by stealth, from behind. Tiger will not attack if it thinks you are watching.
We need to decide quickly. These two...
They broke into a sprint — which ended with Kurup discovering the reason why the two had disappeared.
You’re lucky the dead leaves broke your fall.

b4-p008.t: For leading us into a ditch?
If a stream made this, it came from Mount Dronagiri. Which means this ravine must go up to the base of the mountain.
Rivers encounter obstacles and change course over time
So we can travel through the forest — staying in the ditch — and reach the mountain?
Like me, I suppose. I seemed to have gone underground somewhere and turned up here.
Rivers that go underground become part of mythological folklore. Names no longer matter as they are unreal anyways.
Yes! This is the perfect solution.

b4-p009.t: Come, we’ll take a small detour.
No, we have to keep moving.

The ravine eased upwards and so little of the forest remained that they could see large boulders strewn where mountain met the plains. From atop one such boulder, Dvij espied a close-knit group of temples warmly ensconced in a thicket.
Why are we going to the Mahavidhya temples?
The pujari is old and reticent. He does not meet anyone.
Come along. He will meet us.

b4-p010.t: 'If Shiva is united with Shakti, He can create. If He is not united with Her — He cannot even stir.'
For the Shaktas, Devi is the ultimate Godhead.

An attendant tried to dissuade them — a satsang was in progress. They persisted. The administrator was surly and dismissive. They had no chance — when a tall burly man walked in, gave a start upon seeing them, and immediately intervened.
We have sought your presence, O virtuous one, for it is true knowledge that we seek.

b4-p011.t: We are going up Mount Dronagiri — and she is coming with us.
There are those who do not want us to go up that mountain — those who are after the secret and will misuse it. Evil men who will stop at nothing.
We must not let her get hurt.
The pujari leaned back and nodded, as if he had understood everything.
The attendant stopped fanning and showed them out. They managed one last peek at the reclining pujari before the chamber doors shut.

b4-p012.t: Don’t you ever do that again.
What? Unnerved by the old pujari?
I don’t like being pointed out.
And what was that? Who is going to hurt me?
Nobody. I have made usre of that.
Shortly they were with the rest of the group — where they found an exasperated Kurup, tired from the effort of keeping Ponga from chasing the dog.
It’s getting late. We should find a place to park for the night.
There is a ruined temple a few hundred yards ahead. That would be a good resting spot.
Then let’s head straight to this temple.

b4-p013.t: Bhavi’s thoughts on seeing the temple: there's something about ancient structures that makes them ruin beautifully. Like a new-found love in an old man's life.
Someone spread out sleeping bags, another gathered wood and started a fire, and yet another kept out a vessel to boil tea.
They nestled around the fire and clinked their copper mugs to celebrate the end of the first day of their mission.

Mount Meru is extraordinary. Everything - sun, planets — rotates around it. In Puranas, land is divided into seven continents separated by an ocean: of salt, sugarcane juice, wine, ghee, buttermilk, milk, and sweet water.

b4-p014.t: Yes — the land of jamuns as mighty as elephants. Those jamuns fall on the mountain forming a river of juice — the Jambunadi.
This place is a treasure trove. What is this temple?

While Kurup enchanted the others, Dvij had wandered off to explore. The temple turned out to have an abundance of carvings — ravaged by time, and yet the surviving portions only heightened its appreciation.
This was once the temple of the priest of Kushwaha kings. Some say sage Drona meditated atop this very mountain - praying to Lord Shiva for boons.
I am guessing this is where you picked up the statue for professor.
Prof said there were only 2 of its kind. And you said the other is in the temple. Why is it missing?
The locals must have damaged it. Look - here it is.
How different the same statue looks when it is damaged.

b4-p015.t: I’m going out. I love to listen to the stream's babble.
Listen as much as you want — but do not drink from it. Its water is like poison.
I want to see the rapids froth and foam as they rumble over tumbling rocks. I want to see tiny whirlpools swirl in pools. I want—
You want to walk up the stream with me?
A sequence of deliberate accidents ensued — footsteps momentarily close, then stepped away, only to come close again.
Hands brushed and fingers felt. No more words were spoken.
A late evening mist had descended, covering everything in a thick fog-like translucency.

b4-p016.t: It’s so beautiful. How come you’re not snapping pics?
The next clue on the parchment looked like a coiled serpent.
Cannot be sheshnag as no Lord Krishna dancing on top.
Saving battery in case I catch a signal up above.
What’s that structure over there? A temple?
If you don’t mind clinging on to me - we can cross the stream and find out.
So that is how the stream was conquered — by using the cling-and-cross technique. Dvij was conscious of the tactile pleasure of supporting Bhavi's weight, and was made self-conscious because of that.

The building turned out to be an ancient temple completely draped in vines. Centuries of soil had deposited around it, giving it the appearance of having slightly sunk into the ground. It was likely to have remained untouched for centuries.

b4-p017.t: Before the two pairs of quivering lips could meet, fate intervened in the form of a rustle outside. The stormy face of Yogini was visible in the dim light of the dusk.
What happened back there... I did that to spite that woman.
Bhavi quickly pulled Dvij to her and gave him a long, deep kiss.
Though you are what my uncle would call 'a a gandharva's incarnation.'

Later that night,Dvij dreamt of Professor explaining the five M’s: madya, matsya, mamsa, mudra, maithuna. Finally, his sleeping mind figured out what the coiled serpent in Professor's parchment stood for.

b4-p018.t: Either it had rained or the morning dew was so thick it dripped from the trees, reflecting the sunrise in a million mirrors. The second day of the search had begun.
We go away from the stream. Longer, but far less dangerous.
No, we need to cover ground. We follow the stream.
Did you know, you’ve got a nice smile.
...I will not tell you what the coiled serpent in the parchment means.
This is kundalini! And the elephant— I believe that is one of the chakras.
Dvij had pulled out his cheat sheets — copied from Professor's notes. Each chakra had a shape, a colour, a deity, and an associated animal. The elephant was Vishuddha. The throat chakra.

b4-p019.t: Up there — that is where the Ashtomis live. A legendary race that survives by smelling flowers. They do not eat nor drink. Any unpleasant smell causes instant death.

Suddenly Bhavi stopped. The water was darker at one point than elsewhere. Dvij had seen it too. He gestured: keep moving. There indeed was a drain pipe — embedded in the earth, emerging at the stream's edge, spewing sludge into the water.
My guess — an industrial setup on the other face of the mountain.
This is why people are falling sick. We must do something.
Someone is dumping effluents into the stream. But where?
We will, when the time is right. For now, pretend we don’t know about the spill.

b4-p020.t: The group moving again up the path, Dvij now at Kurup's side in conversation about the mountain's mythologies. Then a tangle of legs — Dvij's foot hooking Kurup's ankle, sending him stumbling forward.
Here — water. I filled it fresh from the stream just now.
Kurup almost goes down. The act looks accidental. Dvij offered his hand, his apologies, and his flask.

Vidgati's shrine. A plateau carved from the mountain centuries ago by a Buddhist settlement long since gone. The Charvakas had made it their home. The party arrived at the end of the second day — dusty, tired, and hungry.

b4-p021.t: I thought they are wriggling tadpoles.
Hush! We know that these figures are 8 of a kind.
Eight of a kind, huh? Could be Ashtalakshmis?
Or ashtamangalas? But no connection to chakras.

b4-p022.t: Let’s look at the next one. Is it a stopwatch? But what could that mean?
That we are running out of time!
While life is yours — live joyously.

Dinner to the locals meant a feast. They drank and passed the wine and talked with their mouths full and sang till one by one they frittered away into the darkness, having lived another day of their lives joyously.

Prakriti is nature. From its latent energies, through stages of evolution, arise the 24 principles — Mahat, cosmic intelligence, ego, mind, the five senses, the organs of action, the subtle and gross elements. It is the absolute philosophy.
The Samkhya wall diagram was like a carved visual philosophy, worn and beautiful. The 24 principles flowing from Prakriti felt like a cosmological map: the universe explaining itself in stone.
Sorry! Err... where can I read Charvaka’s works?
He likes to read. A lot.
The reading room. Go there in the morning.

b4-p023.t: The water you drank from my bottle, that was poisoned from the polluted stream, Kurup.
Oh no, at that point the stream is not—

Kurup stopped abruptly. Sudden fear in his eyes. He said something about being tired and walked off briskly. Dvij stood there grinning. Bhavi stared at both of them. Later in the night, she slipped out and approached Dvij’s hut.
All that food. Sensual indulgence. What's the word for it? Hedonism — yes, that's it.
Good. Now tell what are you hiding from me.
Nothing. Just that you’ll find someone missing in the morning.
He rubbed his stuffed belly again, enjoying the sensation of feeling full. His kundalini had risen to manipura — the solar plexus chakra. The third level.

Bhavi woke up to a loud commotion which sounded like people were on a lookout. By the time Bhavi unfolded the flapped exit from her hut, the commotion had dispersed. Only Dvij stood by, nibbling on a datoon stick.

b4-p024.t: Dvij delicately removed her hand, went to the washing area, rinsed, washed his face. Bhavi's fist was poised dangerously. He laughed.
The stream carries the toxins to the lake. That’s poisoned the land, livestock and the people. It has lost its healing bacteriophages to chemical contamination.
I tripped him — deliberately — to get him preoccupied. Then I offered him water I said I had filled from the stream. I wanted to see if he would drink it.

b4-p025.t: Exactly. Because he knew the water was safe to drink at that point. Because he knows where the pipe is — downstream.
That’s why you were looking at the murthis. So Kurup is Mahant's henchman?

The statue Kurup showed in the temple — it was not the same as the one in Prof's study. I know the mudras of the hands and feet. That statue sits in Mahant's stateroom. I saw it when we were waiting for him.
Kurup found the pipe. He told Mahant. Mahant got bribed by the factory owners and shoved it under the carpet. He offered Kurup protection. A deal was struck.
Then the national park expansion threatened to expose it all. Mahant had to get rid of the park. The Park Commissioner was killed. The tunnel led to his temple.
You mean he had the Park Commissioner killed?

b4-p026.t: That ugly Kabandh! Knowing what is causing it and letting people die.
That would explain the procession of lights we saw the night before we started.
Kurup must have told Mahant about our expedition.
Not only that - now he will share his copy of the parchment with Mahant.
If only I could get my hands on him -
No, prof’s secret is something ancient. That is still hidden in the parchment.
Could the drain pipe be uncle’s secret?
Then there’s only one thing to do. Solve the rest of the clues.

b4-p027.t: What are you doing here, you fool?
Kurup had retraced his steps to the base of the mountain. Mahant had his men set up a camp there. He hesitated before entering Mahant's tent — grander than the others.
They found out about the drain pipe.
Baldev struck him. He fell, taking the curvaceous jar of liquor with him. Mahant cursed — once, twice, three times. Baldev joined the chorus with even more imaginative profanities.
I told you to bring me the parchment.
I have a copy with me.
They have solved just the first couple clues.
We can solve the rest before them.

b4-p028.t: You said they are looking for a leaf. What leaf?
They haven’t figured that out yet.
For your sake, you better not be lying.
Now leave. And don’t show your face again.
Send a party forward. A little scare — not really hurt them. Just delay their progress.
Baldev nodded and stepped out. Kurup was already breathing his relief in the mountain air outside. Mahant caught his reflection in the glass he was drinking from. His eyes were bloodshot.

b4-p029.t: The reading room was a T-shaped structure made entirely of bamboo. Its shelves hung from the ceiling on coir ropes — to defeat the termites below. Dust particles sparkled in the narrow beams of light.
What made you so desperate to see this library?
Kaala — the kanchuka of time limitation. Just like a stopwatch. The stopwatch points to a kanchuka. But we need a lookup table to find which chakra.
Don't ask me to go over the books one more time.
Time passed. Bhavi's head was hurting, her stomach grumbling, and she was on the verge of falling asleep.
We will have to if you want to crack the code.
Each chakra has a bija akshara — a letter of the alphabet associated with the centre of its lotus symbol.
J is the bija akshara of svadhishthana — the sacral chakra.
Two pictures cracked. Only one more to go.
Look, in the periodic table of tattvas - kaala is mapped to letter J.

b4-p030.t: Let’s just say I’ve made provisions.
How can you say that with such confidence?
What if Mahant’s men catch up?
Rest assured. They’ll not be able to hurt you.
Panditji, what is the significance of number 8 in our shastras?

They found the round-nosed man at the precipice, providing an unbounded view of the valley below. Brown transitioning to green. The blue of the lake at the centre. Fields of wheat, barley, cotton. Egrets in the paddies.

Well, let’s see. Three would be the Trimurti — Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva. Four would be the Vedas. But clearly, the most significant number was seven. Objects are arranged in heptads throughout the Rig Veda...
Eight? The Ashtamatrikas — the Varaha Purana includes Yogeshwari as the eighth, representing the eight immoral qualities. I did not think you would know about them.
Yes, yes — but how about eight.
Why, the group of vowels, of course.
The consonants of our alphabet are grouped into seven vargas — each relating to one of the Saptamatrikas.

b4-p031.t: Thank you. Twice in two days you have shown us the right path.
The ashtamatrikas — and the last one relates to the vowels. Each chakra is a lotus with a different number of petals. A letter is assigned to each petal — vrittis.
Wait up. The three chakras are Vishuddha, Svadhishthana and...Vishuddha again? That doesn't seem right.
The vowels are all assigned to the petals of only one lotus. The lotus of Vishuddha chakra.
That’s it. We have solved all of them.
Look carefully — the elephant has seven trunks.
Those are trunks? I thought prof’s hands were shaking when he drew this.
No — clearly seven trunks. And in this table, a seven- trunked elephant maps to muladhara. The base chakra.
— arranged in an upside-down triangle as uncle drew.
So the three chakras are muladhara, svadhishthana and vishuddha -
Both of them took a good look at the design and shook their heads. It made no sense from any angle.

b4-p032.t: I know I should not be laughing - but that is one funny face.
Bhavi drew a second diagram, this time using the shapes associated with the three chakras: a square (muladhara's shape), a crescent (vishuddha), a circle or specific form (svadhishthana).
This is a Vedic altar. These shapes are homa-kundas.
A number of mathematical discoveries were made in ancient times to create these precise altar shapes. Including what is known as the pythagoras theorem.
Is there any place with such homa- kundas?
The ashram of Kritya Rishi — right on the path toward the top.
The ashram has these homa- kundas?
No doubt about it. It is a Vedic ashram after all.
How’s that for solving a clue?
Good. Now we move - in that direction.

b5-p001.t: They walked on paths made by the footsteps of centuries. At each bifurcation they paused only a moment before instinct took them upward.

The journey up till the mid-afternoon meal went eventless. They breathed in the refreshing mountain air at peace. Ponga had to be hurried along occasionally. Bhavi felt, once or twice, as if they were being watched.

Dvij moved ahead with blithesome ease. Bhavi watched his masculine form ascend — then looked askance and saw that Yogini was watching it too. Suddenly the masculine form vanished. Yogini sprang forward. Bhavi began running.
Dvij was hanging in a ravine below — gripping a cluster of aerial roots of a fig tree, his body suspended above the ravine's depth, his grip the only thing between him and the drop.

b5-p002.t: Bhavi's arm fell short by inches. She looked at Yogini — who was already working on the roots with a blunt knife. Their eyes met. Together they looped the cut roots around the ones Dvij hung from.
Together they began pulling. With the combined effort of their grunts and gasps, Dvij inched upward. They lay sprawled at the edge, too exhausted to move —
Thanks, girls. I never thought you’d shed your differences....
- till the inquisitive stare of Ponga, who had painfully made his way up, proved too much for Dvij.
That's right — we'll need to go back and take the other path.

Yogini smiled — the first time he had seen her do so. Bhavi gave him her dagger-like stares, huffed, and started walking back down the slope. Dvij hoped Bhavi would look back. She did, ever so slightly.

b5-p003.t: I should thank you for saving my life.
I had to - both of you helped.
You did thank — both of us.
This time, yes. But I’ve saved you once already.
A loud cry came from behind where they stood. Three men emerged from ambush, daggers shining in their outstretched hands. Yogini had already engaged one of them.
Dvij whipped out a handgun from somewhere in a flash. The thugs halted in their tracks. He asked Bhavi to hide behind a boulder while he held them at bay.
Bhavi saw a thug attack her as she hid behind the boulder. Suddenly, a tall stranger appeared from nowhere and faught off the thug. She had no idea who he was, but he was clearly on her side.
Dvij took off running up the slope as an attacker pursuid. Then both vanished. Bhavi and Yogini ran after them. At the rim: Dvij was hanging from the same aerial roots. For the second time that day.

b5-p004.t: Bhavi nodded at Yogini. No eye-contact needed this time. They went about rescuing Dvij in the same manner — having done it not too long ago. This time he offered no thanks.
I was chasing a thug away.
I wonder who that tall stranger was who fought from our side.
I saw someone chasing you. Looks like both fell in.

Ponga was found lying supine where the thugs had attacked — mildly unconscious. A few drops of water revived him. They rested under the shade of the fig tree whose aerial roots had now saved Dvij twice.
Actually... I forgot about the ravine.
Not for someone who has forgotten his whole past.
I get it that you lured the thug to the ravine. But why did you jump in?
Yoiu forgot about the ravine where you had almost died a few moments ago? That’s stupid.

b5-p005.t: The quiet evening walk — and the dolmen at nightfall. Ahead in a large open field: a dolmen — three upright stones topped with a large capstone, ancient, solid, its shadow long in the last light. The party moves toward it.
Mahant needs us to get him close enough to the secret of the leaf. Till then he will keep following us...
Who knows what he might do after that.
Picked it up from the firearm display case in the Park Commissioner's bungalow.
Thought it would come in useful on a day like this.
How do you know so much about guns?
There’s a fifty percent chance that you are a good guy.

b5-p006.t: In a flashback in Bhavi’s thoughts: Dvij handled the firearms with a fluency he could not account for. 'But don't ask me how,' he said, lifting the rifle in an action-hero pose.
I would care more for that if the gun was not pointed at my face.
These grooves — they impart a spin to the bullet that improves accuracy over a longer range.
Semantic memory is memory of general things — like how to drive a car. Episodic is memory of events — where and when you learned to drive.
You have clearly retained your semantic memory. You know about computers, mobiles, the internet — things that do not exist in this valley.
A second flashback — Professor on semantic and episodic memory. A deeper memory layer, triggered by the gun's fluency: Professor's study, the memory-test conversation.
What picture do I have of him?
Go out there. Listen to the forest. Hear the rumbling hills. Do things — and your body will tell you what you know. Eventually you will have the complete picture of yourself.

b5-p007.t: Don’t worry about the gun. There are no bullets.
Yes, that was weighing on my mind. Good you took them out.
I did not take them out. There never were any.
What? You were bluffing with our lives at stake?
It's a good thing she's with us. I feel safe knowing she's keeping a watch.
When you were brought to the lodge, you were still conscious despite all the blood you had lost.
Like the tantric baba said - she must have done something that kept you alive. Both of us helped.
Fireflies! We are sleeping in a field of fireflies.

b5-p008.t: Anahata. I can hear the sound of the unstruck.

Slowly silence descends on everything. The stream stops murmuring. The tall grass stop swishing. Yogini and the dog go still. The owl in the forest below stops calling. The great silence — and the sound of the unstruck.
Much later, Dvij watched Bhavi sleeping peacefully under the ancient dolmen in a field of fireflies. Then, making sure she was asleep, he crept quietly toward where Yogini lay.
...good enough to wake any sleeping soul.
Where did you get the milk?
No milk, no sugar. Dark as the devil.

b5-p009.t: He will help us with the time comes. I’m sure.
Why, he seems to recognize this leaf.
Why did uncle want Ponga to come with us?
Those thugs. Will they attack us again?
In all these years, you’ve feared for Prof, but never for your own. Ever wonder why?
Soon, they reached the Vedic ashram of Kritya Rishi. Bamboo-and-thatch huts, swastikas above every entrance.
The altar with the vedi at its centre, surrounded by the three homa- kundas. Square. Circular. Crescent. Exactly as Bhavi had drawn it.
The udgatrus began. Their Samaveda chants created the cosmic vibes of the apaurusheya Vedic texts.
Some singers, enraptured, broke into dancing. Others took up the naali and dundhubi. The ceremony had begun.
Just outside the ashram, Bhavi had discovered a bountiful garden. She moved from tree to tree like a buzzing bee busy collecting their nectar.

b5-p010.t: The Vedas are apaurusheya — ever-present, all- encompassing, received by the ancient rishis.
They are shrauta texts, preserved by oral recitation. Upanishads act as mediums of esoteric interpretation.
Punarmrityu — re-death. We die again in the beyond, only to be born again. The endless cycle of samsara.
Nachiketas learned how to conquer this cycle from Lord Yama. As the river disappears into the sea, we become one into the divine.
Svetaketu — split the fruit. Split its seed. Keep splitting. That invisible essence left at the end is Brahman.
In ashwamedha yagya, the horse is the sun. It’s body is time. The sacrifice is that of worldly comforts.
Thank you, swamiji. I now see the world in a way I had never seen before. But my mind remains restless. I shall come and seek more.
Place salt in water. Taste it — present but invisible. Similarly Brahman can be experienced but not observed. Tat tvam asi.

b5-p011.t: Yes, else my mind will remain restless.
Is meeting the maharishi that important?
I have heard you tell many that you seek the truth. I never thought you actually meant it.
I did not. But now, I think I do.
And second. Find a safe spot. Away from the ashram.
What’ll I do the 2 hours you are gone?
Two things. First - work on next clue.
Dvij turned and walked back toward the ashram. The Maharishi would address his disciples at 4 pm. There were things he still needed to ask.
As she saw Dvij's receding figure, Bhavi was worried that the man she had barely begun to know was already becoming a different person. Then she shrugged. She looked around for Ponga.

b5-p012.t: We will rest under the boulders tonight.

They travelled on a path that circled above the ashram. Bhavi saw a safe spot between three large boulders that rested on each other. It gave them cover, a vantage point, and a clear view of the ashram below.
Now, the next clue. What are these? Nine green eyes? Why are they splotchy?
I will take that as a yes.
Wait — those stems in uncle's room. The green is from those pressed stem-ends.
Beans! Green beans. That's moong! Even maharaj could tell that.
These cannot be eyes. Maybe something we eat — small, round, bean-shaped—

b5-p013.t: My dear Ponga — will you please stop staring at the heavens and help me with why nine?
The heavens! Navgrahas! Nine planets! Why did I not think of it before?
I saw a navgraha puja once. Pujari asked for green beans as it was a Wednesday. Each navgraha has its own grain. This clue points to Wednesday.
I can’t wait to see the look on Dvij’s face.
But which Wednesday? What day is it today? How long has it been since we started?
She decided she had done enough and went back to meet Dvij in the garden — leaving Ponga continuing to ponder the heavens.

b5-p014.t: A circle. Like the Laxman rekha.

Bhavi had been waiting too long. Dark clouds gathered in the west. Birds stopped chattering. She could hear a strange sound — sonorous, guttural — arriving from the depths of the woods. Before she knew it, she was running.
Why were you running like that? I almost died of fright.
And I thought I was scared.
It sent shivers down my spine. Why can’t they sing to themselves?
That'll be uhya gaana — secret singing.
Aranya gaana. Someone is singing sacred mantras in contemplation.
I’ve solved the next clue. And mind you - did not need any of your no cheat sheets.
By the end of her explanation, Dvij appeared genuinely appreciative of what she had done.

b5-p015.t: Let’s see. Moong maps to Budha — yes. But also to: the element earth, metal brass, gem emerald..
It's a leaf. Green is bound to be everywhere.
So we need to move northwards. Let’s ask the ashram people for directions.
Wait. The directions. Each graha presides over a direction. Budha has north.
Too risky. Mahant’s men will force the information out from them. We need to find north ourselves.
And for that, we will build a gnomon.

A gnomon. A stick, a rope, and a sharp end. The shadow at dusk marks east. Tomorrow at dawn, the shadow crosses the circle again — that marks east too. Two points. Then two arcs. They intersect. Draw the line through the intersection — that's north.
Ash from cow dung is a good mosquito repellent. No smell.

b5-p016.t: For all his supposed insanity, the man sometimes seems saner than us.
Dvij thought of the power of chanting mantras. The acts of cleansing by Agni. The doctrine of twice-dead. Did his kundalini rise to vishuddha state?
Think of the happiness of the people in the valley.
Too cloudy. It wouldn’t have worked anyways.
I thought we were desperate for rains.
A day! Couldn’t the rains have waited just one more day?
Where did he get the rudraksha mala from?
Chill, we’ll work something out. Be like Ponga. Still.

b5-p017.t: Bhavi watched the two men gesticulate wildly and could only imagine the words being exchanged. The charade ended when Dvij extracted the rosary from Ponga's tightly clasped hand.
Rudraksha has magnetic properties. A stalk full of them must align along the earth's magnetic field.
Which means the path we have to take is that one — the one flanked by bakul trees.

b5-p018.t: Sharp cries rose from over the ridge. Armed men with lathis had charged inside the ashram. The huts started collapsing. The ashram dwellers were rounded up. The first act of vandalism was complete.
Mahant entered flanked by Baldev. The sadhu had fallen at his feet in beseeching. Mahant kicked him and stormed off to beneath the large banyan tree. Baldev tagged behind like a monkey's tail.
Good we did not tell the ashram people about our whereabouts.
He is working out the direction from the clues himself.
Looks like he’s worked it out. But why are they headed south?
That’s odd. My parchment has black beans, not green.
Green maps to north. I’m sure of it.

b5-p019.t: I changed it to different colors when I created copies. To sniff our treachery.
So mine is black, and Kurup’s must be red. Which maps to south.
That’s why they are heading south.
This is brillant. Now they can never catch us.
We have Mahant out of our way.
Then what are we waiting for — let's go!
Rousing Ponga from his meditative state, they quickly embarked on the path that radiated northwards from the Vedic ashram. The bakul trees stood on either side. The mountain waited above.

b5-p020.t: This climb is like trying to find the end of Shiva’s column of fire... unending.
My worry is that we are looking for a plant... and we have left most of them behind.
The path ascended so rapidly it appeared to be headed toward the heavens. Most vegetation had been left behind. The air was getting rarer.
How does the old man keep going?
Look — up there. A small temple. We can rest there.
His sense of purpose, I suppose.

A small Hanuman temple, white with a vermillion base. A trident with a damroo at its nape. And beside it, under the spreading tree: a monk in meditative stillness, his face carrying an aura of enlightenment.
Dvij looked quizzically at an equally surprised Bhavi. He walked around and humbly addressed the perfectly seated monk. Bhavi knelt beside him. The monk's words fell like rain on dry ground.

b5-p021.t: You seek the Absolute Truth. And yet you do not know that you already possess it.
Just like a devotee who seeks God but does not know God is already within him.
You have forgotten — just like an accident makes the a man forget his own past.
How can one renounce the world? What else is there but feelings?
Can you teach me the Truth?
I can show you the way.
I am a reflection of your soul that has been wandering in vacuum...
...having lost its association with the mind that makes it realise its purpose.
The climb had drained Bhavi. The cool breeze and the monk's discourse had calmed her into sleep. She had missed most of what was discussed.
Oh, I know this one. A bull with two legs is Dwaparyuga.
He asked me to look within.
Not before you look at the next clue.

b5-p022.t: Satyuga is a complete bull — four legs. Treta has three, Dwapar two, Kali one.
You’re not the only one who reads uncle’s books.
Now, this man forms a perfect square — head at north-east, feet at south-west.
This has to be vaastu purusha - the cosmic man.
Good. But what about the fish? Mina - pisces?
The rashis preside over specific organs. Like, Mesha controls the head...
...Karka the chest, Makara the knees... and Mina the feet.
The feet of the vaastu purusha!
And the Dwaparyuga bull — it also maps to the afternoon kala at the Vedic ashram. The third prahara. 3 to 6 pm.
Vaastu places a library where the feet are. And it says to be there from 3 to 6 pm in the pursuit of knowledge.
What could happen under the shade of this tree?
That’s double confirmation! Something will happen here between 3 to 6 pm.
I know... shadows. They will elongate and point us in the right direction.

b5-p023.t: The they looked at the shadows. The afternoon light was already angling westward. The shadows were beginning to lengthen.
It's Lord Shiva! He will show us the way!!
Why...it's...it's the shadow of the trishul!

Dvij folded out a bedspread. Bhavi laid out food. Ponga plucked wild berries from shrubs, popping handfuls into his mouth, spat out the kernels in a well-practiced arc. They sat in the sun, watching Ponga without trying to understand him.
Why is he punching holes in this bottle?

b5-p024.t: I know what the secret is.
I can. Whose temple are we sitting next to—
The shadow's tip was clearly in the middle of a narrow path leading into the field of rocks. They leapt up and ran.
None of the plants had leaves that matched Professor's drawing. Bhavi was rapidly getting worked up being faced with the prospect of failure.
The plant must have been here earlier. This wild weed - it’s an invasive species. Maybe it wiped it out.

b5-p025.t: I wish we could take the whole mountain - like Lord Hanuman.
What’s he doing up in the tree?
He’s got a moth in a bottle?
The trapped male moth will release chemicals - like a brassy perfume. Females will come to the bottle.
Oh, right! So prof knew that we will need Ponga for this...

b5-p026.t: Nervous minutes passed that felt like a lifespan. Then the moths arrived — at first few, then many, then a swarm streaming from over the boulder wall. They stumbled over the boulders, helping each other upward as quickly as they could.
We did it! We did it!!
They found themselves at the top of the hammock, looking at a field where white flowers swayed in the winds that rushed in from the chasm beyond.
What herb was Lord Hanuman looking for when he carried away the whole mountain?
Who the tall stranger who fought the thugs...?
Sent by the pujari to protect of Mahavidya temples you. He's the doyen of the shakta tradition.
You embody the Goddess. He would not let you be harmed.

b5-p027.t: Before Dvij could reply, his phone rang, the shrill ringtone reverberating in the vastness. Bhavi saw him lift the phone, and then letting it slip from his palm. She could almost hear it crash against rock, then tumble down and vanish.
Bhavi looked at his face eager to detect any emotion. All she found was serenity — as if enwrapped by a translucent layer of bliss. Anandmaya kosha, she thought.
The rain clouds moved toward the valley. The white flowers swayed in the wind from the chasm. The phone was gone. The past was gone. What remained was this.

b5-p028.t: Bhavi was reminded of the stories of the nymphatic apsara and the ascetic rishi that she had heard as a child. She had the strange feeling of being alone in the entire world sweep over her.
Are you going to leave me alone?
In Yogini you shall find a true friend. In the Mahavidya priest, the strongest of allies.
You are the only one who can stop Mahant.
Close the drainpipe. Rally the peasants. Heal them with this herb.
I am a seeker. Seekers do not become good healers. You, on the other hand, are selfless.

b5-p029.t: My kundalini has risen to ajna — the brow chakra. But there are seven extra-sensory chakras. I have to keep moving towards the Truth.

Dvij turned before the tearful face of his beloved Bhavi became a deterrent to his tireless pursuit. He climbed down the boulders. He started walking up the path through the valley of the white flowers that seemed to reach out into nothingness.
A slim black and white chatak made a string of whistling notes as it flapped its wings and merged into the darkness of the gathering clouds. The faithful dog followed him like certain Death.
